## 16. SEC7: advice that reaches the builder

Implementer: Codex for Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22. Wave-22 commission;
DX6 owns session/upgrade/clock and frontend/proof-kit fixes. No version bump.
This section supersedes §15.2's special display cap for insert/result notes and
§12.3's advisory-only boundary only for the two explicit gates below.
It also revises §§13.5/14.2/14.5/14.6: disposition-clearable review gates are
a new exit-1 category alongside replayed intent violations, including without
invariants. Their zero-new-refusal bars continue to bind failures no disposition
can clear (compilation failures and reachable refutations). Gate counts and
legitimate review costs are reported separately, never called replayed exploits. Runtime
authority and the proved/refuted/unproved contract remain unchanged.

### 16.1 Presentation and conditional questions

A shared severity ordering puts gated notes and likely-hole questions before
coverage, restates and result inventories. Default check retains every priority
0–2 likely-hole question and the first five ordinary code classes in severity
order, keeping each selected class's distinct sites/audiences; SEC6 insert/result
notes never increase that budget. Result exposure notes group by source table, retaining every operation,
column, observer kind and source site in JSON/full text. Audit uses the same
severity and numeric file/line/column ordering, never lexicographic site strings.
Insert-write advice requires an explicitly supplied nonliteral expression whose
flow uses a mutation argument; omitted defaults and literal-only assignments are
quiet. These are precision changes to advice, never creation-policy inference.

New advisory classes ask about: reason text without a positive non-whitespace
minimum; optional money supplied to creation; constant true payment/approval
flags (a naming heuristic, explicitly a question); competing generic enum setters
versus stricter literal transitions; mutable creation checks omitted by a later
transition or derived creation; inconsistent server-now duration bounds on the
same bound column across operations; and global-role operations recording viewer
on an unrelated row. Restating questions and the draft ask whether each role may
write any row, independently of the read questionnaire. The relationship recipe
models the owner of this wall explicitly. These shapes cannot infer the spec.

### 16.2 Narrow gates and individual dispositions

N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE: an optional image/file mutation argument flows to an
insert/upsert of a media column, including a conditional child insertion. A
non-null guard around just the child does not establish required parent evidence.
An unconditional dominating require of non-null before any creating write can
exclude the note; aliases/helpers are resolved by the existing authority walker.
Optionality may be intentional: the gate requires review, never asserts an exploit.

N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT: a read branch trusts a retained grant; an authored grant
writer requires a literal role on the principal argument stored as that grant's
reader principal; that role is mutable through authored operations; and the read
branch does not imply the same current-reader role. Require a positive recipient
role atom in every admitting writer branch; do not mistake the assigner's role
for the recipient's. The gate excludes ordinary owner branches, literal service
seats and mere caller-role requirements. Revoking derived grants is a repair;
static inability to prove full revocation remains reviewable, not an automatic
safety theorem. General N_GRANT_OUTLIVES_ROLE stays advisory.

Unreviewed gates make check exit 1 with structured note IDs, without marking an
invariant refuted. The existing bulk --ack-notes cannot clear a security gate.
Use check --ack-security <id> --reason '<spec rationale>' for one current note.
Store versioned dispositions in snapback/security-reviews.json with ID, reason,
source digest and analyzer revision. IDs hash the complete diagnostic; the source
digest hashes all compiled source filenames and bytes in sorted order. Every
source edit, changed diagnostic or analyzer revision invalidates the disposition.
Blank reasons, unknown IDs, malformed files and incompatible flag combinations
refuse. Writes use temp+rename and verify compiled sources still match disk;
failed compilation/refuted intent must never record acknowledgments. Dispositions
are review records, never authority or proof, remain visible in JSON/audit and
can be checked into source control. Broad advice may also be individually reviewed.

### 16.3 Directed finite histories

Keep the 512 breadth/pair budget. Add a separate bounded directed frontier before
breadth exploration for schema enum transitions and mutable dependencies of
independent intent/creator checks. Generate successors from the current world,
so references returned/created at one step are available later. Track semantic
state signatures over status/role/boolean/relationship fields, rather than minted
IDs alone; prioritize unseen lifecycle signatures and schema-relevant mutations.
Bound depth to eight authored mutations, attempts to 2048 and retained frontier
to 16 worlds; share check's existing work/deadline cap and report every cut.
Actual mutation admission, executed-write judgments and ordinary observers remain
the only failure oracle. Synthetic witnesses remain REVIEW and never failures.
Validated generated initial fixtures retain their explicit provenance. No seed
state is relabeled application reachable, and finite exhaustion remains unproved.

### 16.4 Qualification

Regression tests cover positive and negative shapes, helper/alias guards,
per-note/source/analyzer invalidation, failed-check non-writing, severity and
numeric ordering, and lifecycle/suspension histories beyond pairs. Measure every
wave-22 schema's default visibility and waves 15,16,18–22's gate counts separately
from false refusals. Optional evidence can legitimately fail pending a disposition;
report that cost explicitly rather than claim every gate is a confirmed hole.
Re-run copies of the eight high lanes without intent, with authored intent, and
with one independent spec-worded invariant. Advice is flagged; only a replayed
violation is caught. Packed qualification executes every changed guide snippet.

### 16.5 Review clarification: exact detector and command boundaries

These details resolve design review M1–M6. The implementation is the bounded
shape detector, not an inference that a schema satisfies its product specification.

Priority codes are fixed by security::note_priority: gates at 0; privilege and
self-claimed relationship at 1; grant-outlives, optional evidence, role-wide read,
broad read, caller time, sweep deadline and the seven new question codes at 2;
ordinary notes at 4; insert/result inventory at 5; restates at 6; intent coverage
at 7. The short list keeps every action at 0–2 plus the first five ordinary
code classes, preserving all sites/audiences within those classes. Repeated sites
of one ordinary code do not consume independent classes; insert/result codes
never enlarge the budget. This avoids hiding a second scan audience or a distinct
maintain diagnostic behind repeated bootstrap notes. Concrete
reachable refutations still print all failing sites, origins and repair commands
outside this list. A remainder count points to verbose/JSON. JSON retains every
note. Restates and coverage can appear only after the action classes fit.

Creation reason: an argument flows into an inserted/upserted column with `reason`
in its case-insensitive name and its text argument minimum is absent or zero.
Optional money: the optional argument flows into an optional Money column, or an
Int/IntRange/Decimal column whose lowercased name contains price, charge, fee or
amount. Constant approval: true literal assigned to a creating column containing
paid, approv or payment. All are name-based specification questions; no claim
covers other spellings. Required positive-minimum reasons and required money
arguments suppress their respective advice. One note per operation/column.

Transition bypass: same-table enum update from an enum argument can choose a
literal also written by another mutation, and its necessary effective admission
does not imply that other writer's bound requirements plus table gate. Resolve
row-local read operands to the target table's focal row for this advisory query.
A dominating contradictory literal argument guard excludes that target. Generic
setter/table/target/stricter-op duplicates collapse by exact diagnostic message.
A stricter-gate failure alone is advisory, never an inferred approval violation.
Stale creation: a resolved creating-write context reads a non-role dependency
that another mutation updates/upserts/deletes, and a different later mutation
updates the created table or writes a referencing child without reading that
dependency in its dominating context. Group by operation, created table and
dependency. Mere dependency reads do not prove eligibility; this heuristic's
false negatives and speculative questions are not gated.
Duration: compare the same resolved table/column against now +/- literal duration
with the same inequality direction in two operation contexts. Different offsets
produce one question listing all windows/operations. Other affine expressions,
custom wrappers and complex derived windows remain uncovered by this advice.
Role-wide write: a mutation updates a non-immutable Principal to viewer, has a
bound global role requirement, and lacks a dominating viewer-to-row-member
relationship comparison. It asks about this resource rather than declaring an
unauthorized write. The draft is bounded by discovered schema roles × tables;
it asks every pair about write authority, including pairs with authored intent.

Optional upload: the existing lexical authority walker resolves aliases and
helper arguments to the original mutation argument. Non-null suppression accepts
only a direct positive `argument != null` conjunct in an unconditional Require
before the first creating-write context. `$advice` branch guards cannot suppress;
late child guards, OR, unknown and unsupported expressions cannot suppress.
Known flows into asset fields are detected; arbitrary opaque/derived flows are
uncovered, never assumed safe. Both upsert arms retain the creation review question.
Retained role: use existing lints::mutable_role and privilege role-column/probe
resolution. Only direct positive Exists conjuncts with a literal recipient role
qualify, never an assigner/viewer-only test or negation. A branch suppresses only
when kernel::implies(branch, recipient-role-with-viewer) is Ok(true); false,
unknown and cap exhaustion retain the question. Dynamic role requirements stay
in general grant advice and are outside the narrow gate. Every noted branch
contains a positive grant probe binding that grant's principal column to viewer.
Owner equalities without such probes are excluded structurally. Role mutation
plus transactional grant revocation still needs review; it is not statically
proved safe or automatically refused as an exploit.

Disposition format is version 1: entries maps full diagnostic SHA256 IDs to
{sources, analyzer, reason}. JSON uses the existing Diagnostic serialization and
the sorted Vec<(filename, UTF-8 source bytes)> serialization used by Project.sources;
source names are schema-directory-relative (`name.q`). A line shift changes the
ID; any source edit changes all dispositions. This intentionally conservative
invalidation avoids unmodeled cross-table influence; optimization is deferred.
Analyzer is the explicit security_reviews::ANALYZER revision, bumped whenever
security detector meaning or disposition identity changes. A release alone does
not invalidate unchanged analysis. A reason must contain non-whitespace text.
No unrelated refuted invariant can be bypassed: any reachable refutation prevents
all acknowledgement writes and check still exits 1. Compilation errors likewise
write no security review. Read-only inspection remains available. Bulk --ack-notes
never addresses these records. --ack-security requires --reason and refuses
combination with --ack-notes, --fix, --store, --release, --emit-lean or --audit;
--json, --verbose, --cost and current-source fixture/residency inspection may
combine. Broad-advice dispositions change display, never exit status. Audit exits
on refuted intent as before and includes all notes/dispositions; new gates fail
check only. Deploy/preview/--strict keep §15.3; we recommend running check in acceptance before
deploy. Saved-source portability is not claimed for dispositions.

Directed exploration is primarily a test campaign: check retains the common
512-work/1500ms cap and may cut before it. No promise grants both directed and
breadth paths their full caps under check. Test retains its 512 singles/pairs
in addition to the directed bound. Successors fork the current complete fixture
through Engine::fork_fixture with its asset ledger; they use ordinary mutate,
NOW and existing executed/observer judgments. The signature keeps enum/bool/
principal/reference fields (with multiplicity), discarding other payload only as
a pruning heuristic. Such mergers and every frontier/argument/successor/depth cut
are explicitly uncovered. Retain up to four priority worlds (below the 16 maximum),
prefer changed enum states and true booleans, at most two new worlds per op/world,
four argument tuples, eight mutations and 2048 actual attempts. These finite
heuristics neither prove reachability nor clear an unproved verdict. Synthetic
matrix probes stay REVIEW; ordinary admitted histories from validated generated
initial fixtures retain GeneratedFixtureTrace and failure eligibility (§14).

Wave-22 high lanes are 004,011,021,026,030,037,040,044. Frozen source copies and
independent spec variants are in tests/security/wave22; the measurement manifest
records SHA256s. 037 remains the specification judgment case. With no invariants,
expect corresponding new/advisory notes on the seven nonjudgment lanes. Spec tests
must catch 026's terminal pickup and 030's suspend-before-approval history, alongside
existing 004/021/037 catches; 040/044 always/absent-money limits stay explicit.
Gate calibration targets: 021 for retained role; 003,018,027,040 for optional
uploads on wave22. 027 may be legitimate optionality: gate cost is review pending,
not a confirmed hole. Across waves15,16,18–22 report every project that fails a gate,

never relabel legitimate review gates zero false positives. Changed executable

### 16.6 Second-review resolutions

The two new gates are check-CI-only review obligations. Deploy still lists all
security notes in §15.3 review; its --strict boundary remains replayed refutations.
Running check in deployment acceptance is recommended, not an enforced fresh-check
receipt protocol. No saved-source deployment claim is made for these dispositions.
Acknowledged gates plus no other errors/refutations give exit 0. Default output
replaces each acknowledged note with its ID/code/reason review record; verbose,
JSON and audit retain the full note. Broad dispositions have this same display
effect with no exit-code effect. Stale entries remain in the file for review
history but do not acknowledge any current note. `check --json`, `check --verbose`
and audit inspect current notes without writing a disposition; malformed files
refuse with repair text. There is no wildcard or bulk security acknowledgment.

IDs use deterministic recursively key-sorted JSON diagnostic values; source digest
uses sorted source pairs. Tests require same-input/same-ID stability on repeated
checks in addition to invalidation controls. The analyzer revision is a reviewed
constant; changes to detector semantics or fingerprint serialization must bump it
and their tests must reject a previous revision. It is not a runtime security
boundary or promise that arbitrary modified binaries honor review semantics.

Transition advice emits only on definite Ok(false) implication, suppressing unknown
or capped comparisons as uncovered by that heuristic. Stale-creation, reason,
money, constant-approval and duration advice use finite structural matches only:
unknown/unsupported syntax does not match and is not inferred safe. Their documented
naming/type/binding fragment is their entire coverage, without a proof claim.
General retained-grant advice and the narrow gate may co-fire intentionally:
count gate projects by gated code and project, not total note count. Neither
advisory repeat creates another required disposition. This preserves existing
conditional-lifetime explanations while identifying the precise required review.

Successor generation, schema/program/actor ordering, argument tuples and stable
priority ties are deterministic for fixed inputs. Time/work cuts remain explicit.
Root generated populations are visited before derived creators mutate their
status/eligibility. This is a validated generated initial fixture, with the same
explicit GeneratedFixtureTrace origin; no root rows are invented terminal states.
The additional pre-transition pass is full-test-only, shares the campaign's
observer ceilings, and never runs recursively or increases check's budget.

SEC7 design review provenance: [verbatim reviews](./reviews/3000.036.004-sec7-review-record.md).

Implementation-review clarifications: upload suppression intersects the positive
non-null requirements of every creating-write context, rather than borrowing one
branch's guards. Recipient probes distinguish the original viewer from the stored
recipient, verify the roster principal column and retain only its literal role
requirement for current-role comparison. Result identity adds to existing source
lineage; it never replaces copied protected-column provenance. Role-wide-write
suppression requires a structural positive viewer-to-target relationship equality.
Directed search includes mutable role/boolean/relationship dependencies, uses two
prioritized actors per tuple (others remain in breadth), and immediately drops
displaced beam worlds. The retained-world high-water mark and shared directed
attempt counter are reported. Disposition writers serialize read-modify-write
through a kernel file lock in ignored generated output, with automatic release
on exit. These are precision/resource corrections within the reviewed contract.

Corpus calibration additionally narrows the retained-role gate to reader probes
whose declared key binds the stored recipient principal to viewer. A parent row
looked up by resource id with an additional owner/customer/parent equality is an
ownership relationship, not this assignment-key gate. The old declared-intent
principal-branch advisory is removed for the same reason; broad retained-grant
advice remains conditional. On wave22 this removes the owner-row questions from
001/009/041 while retaining 021's driver assignment. Directed argument selection
varies bool/enum decision arguments independently on resource identity tuples;
noise text cannot correlate a resource id with just the false branch. Successor
selection keeps distinct priority resource states, not the first two audit-actor
variants. Recipient bindings include implicit upsert-key columns, and effective
column read branches are checked with their row and owner gates. Directed
argument grouping and role-class actor deduplication each record uncovered
alternatives even when their subsequent numeric caps are not reached. The
empty-world directed pass defers population to ordinary generated
initialization/breadth. All omitted populations and variants remain uncovered.

### 16.7 Reviewed optionality in the stock social template

The existing social template intentionally permits text messages without photos.
Ship its single pre-reviewed source/analyzer-bound optional-photo disposition as
ordinary template data, with that explicit reason. This uses the same per-note
file and invalidation as user reviews, never a detector exemption or automatic
acknowledgment of arbitrary notes. The record names only that exact diagnostic
and schema; template/analyzer changes invalidate it and fail starter qualification
until reviewed again. Init beside an existing authored schema does not install
this stock-source disposition. The template README explains the decision. Packed
starter qualification must run init/check unchanged and verify the record becomes
stale after a source edit. No social API or runtime authority changes.

### 16.8 Typed upsert key binding

An unrelated unique index of the same arity must not erase a retained-recipient
grant question. The compiler already resolves positional keys by their types;
the security detector must consume that selected write-target index, not repeat
an arity-only approximation. Cache compiled write-target read-site indexes by
canonical source site and table once per source analysis. When they identify one
index, align the source write's named/positional key expressions with that bound
index's columns and merge the implicit stored fields with its explicit payload.
Keep the existing source pin resolver as a fallback for unambiguous source forms.
No planner/runtime rule or authorization changes: this repairs advice/gate recall
for the already documented shape. A two-unique-index recipient-key regression
and a reader that rechecks the role pin the gate and its suppression. Re-measure
the corpus for any newly recognized gates and report their individual review cost.

### 16.9 Day-two precision and destructive evidence questions

Implementer: Codex for Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22; commissioned by the wave-23
day-two addendum. This supersedes the upload shape and stock-template disposition
in §§16.2/16.5/16.7 and narrows stale-creation advice. It changes analysis and
finite witness selection, never runtime admission or application authority.

**Optional uploads.** Optional arguments and optional columns are a valid model,
including deliberate v2 loosening and exceptions such as a lockout without proof.
Do not gate them merely because their names suggest evidence. Gate an optional
image/file argument flowing to a creating media column only when that column is
required, or a direct positive conjunct of an authored `table always` invariant
requires that exact column to be non-null. Conjunctions may be flattened; an OR,
negation, unrelated column, comment, product document or unknown predicate is not
a mandatory-media declaration. No natural-language specification parsing, deploy
diff exemption, lane exemption or new intent language is introduced. Required
child media with optional arguments remains covered: a guard around only the
child cannot establish evidence at parent creation. Existing dominating non-null
guards across every creating context still suppress the question. Required media
with required arguments needs no optional-upload review. Existing generic optional
evidence advice remains advisory. Bump the analyzer revision; remove the stock
social disposition and its special injection/custody code, because intended
text-only messages now check without any acknowledgment, including after edits.
Keep individual source-bound reviews for the two genuine gated shapes.

**Stale eligibility.** Match a creator's dominating condition on a non-role,
non-immutable column that another authored mutation actually changes (or an
existence condition on a deletable dependency). A mere read of an immutable owner
or an unrelated write to that table is not mutable eligibility. A later operation
qualifies only when it writes an approval-like literal enum state (`approved`,
`accepted`, `authorized`, `granted`, `issued`, `active`, `confirmed`, `paid`,
`signed`) or a true approval/authorization flag, and updates the created table
or creates a directly referencing child. An arbitrary edit, inspection, rejection,
cleanup or status-copy is outside this name-based advisory fragment. Rechecking
the relevant dependency suppresses that path. Group all creator and later-write
sites into one question per created table and mutable dependency; name both sets
of operations and eligibility columns. This is a question, not an assertion that
every such decision must repeat the check; unsupported forms stay uncovered.

**Create/edit asymmetry.** Add `N_CREATE_EDIT_ASYMMETRY`, ranked with likely-hole
questions (priority 2), and `N_PRIVATE_CREATE_EDIT_ASYMMETRY` at priority 1
for a write-only private payload. Compare
argument-supplied creation fields with actual authored updates to that field.
Generic table-wide differences remain ordinary insert inventory; the new classes
require a recovered column-specific conditional guard. Besides stable global
requirements and table update gates, recover a conditional
column guard of the form `if newValue != target.column: require authority`
(or the equivalent equality/else form). Resolve lexical aliases and helper
arguments. Match the exact table, selected target keys, column and assigned
expression; a guard for a different row/field cannot become this column's edit
guard. Only guaranteed leading requirements of the changed branch count. Mixed
conditions, unknown effects and guards separated by intervening writes do not
establish this match. This extraction is isolated to advice; it is not a proof
rule or a new runtime check. Emit only a definite failed implication from creation
admission to the stable edit guard; unknown/capped comparisons do not establish
asymmetry. Group by creator/table/column/guard, name the editor and exact guard.
Suppress the older generic insert-inventory note for the same column so it cannot
obscure the more specific question; defaults/literals remain quiet. A private
write-only escalation requires a definite failed implication from creator
admission to an explicit column-read gate, not merely an unknown read audience.
The message names that audience and asks whether this caller should initialize
the agency's private field. Both forms remain advisory and never infer the spec.

**Non-null witnesses.** Within the existing finite argument and campaign budgets,
prioritize non-null values for optional arguments directly supplying a declared
column-write intent before the null baseline. Preserve null alternatives and
explicit truncation notices. Only actual admitted writes judged against independent
intent refute; finite failure to find a witness remains unproved. Pin a non-null
042 billing-note witness without changing its runtime rule or fabricating a row.

**Evidence removal.** Add advisory priority-2 `N_EVIDENCE_REMOVAL` for a media child
linked to a parent where the creation operation supplies required media and also
creates the parent, or independent parent `always exists child[...]` intent names
that relationship. Identify authored deletes, changes to the parent-reference
column, and explicit null/empty writes to evidence constrained non-null/nonempty
by independent intent. Group by child/parent-reference and list the media fields
and removing operations. Required media types alone do not prove the parent needs
at least one child; phrase this distinction explicitly. Ask whether the last
required evidence row can be removed, and point to a transactional last-child
guard, replacement, parent retirement, and independent integrity intent plus test.
Ordinary replacements of one non-null image are not removals. An optional
attachment with neither required-creation structure nor independent integrity
intent is outside the detector. A source guard may make removal intentional;
this is reviewable advice, not a gate or a claim that the guard is absent.

Qualification pins all twelve wave-23 loosen lanes (including 003's conditional
exception) with zero optional-upload gates; retains required-child and explicit
non-null positive controls; pins a single focused 030 eligibility question,
042's owner-only billing guard and non-null witness, and 028's removal question.
Run corpus measurements before/after, report gate and advice counts separately,
and requalify the packed security guide/starters. Mac verification uses the named
Studio worktree only; SSH unavailability is reported, never counted as a pass.

## Summary

Snapback 4 is one of two parallel candidates for the successor to Snapback 2,
and the sibling of Snapback 3, not its successor. It builds
[LLP 2000.000](./2000.000-keep-the-core-flip-two-substrates.rfc.md) as
written: the Snapback 2 core kept verbatim, two substrates flipped up front —
resources metered at runtime instead of priced statically, and a client that
replicates the viewer's declared partition instead of caching receipted
results — proved first on the hub fixture, with a deterministic simulator as
the primary harness. Snapback 3 ([LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md), led by
Codex / GPT-6 Astra) keeps the same two questions open and discovers their
answers in its first slice. Snapback 2 ([LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md))
continues as the incumbent and the control. All three are judged by one
pre-registered comparison on one clock.

This document records the author's decisions of 2026-09-12 that created the
track, restates the bet on one page so a reader can orient without the brief,
fixes the bakeoff protocol, draws the fence, and plans the first four weeks.
The design argument and its evidence stay in LLP 2000.000. Only running code
will bind (`rules/RULES.md`).

## 1. Decisions (author, 2026-09-12)

On 2026-09-12 Charlie Cheever asked whether Claude Fable 5.1 should lead a
Snapback 4 while Codex / GPT-6 Astra leads Snapback 3 and Snapback 2
continues, "and see which one turns out best." The lead answered yes with
conditions; the author accepted them ("Sounds good") and asked for this
document. The decisions below are therefore the lead's proposal as accepted
by the author. Where the author has not separately ruled, the text says so.

1. **Three tracks, one comparison.** Snapback 2 continues as the incumbent
   and the control. Snapback 3 builds LLP 2000; Snapback 4 builds LLP
   2000.000. This is a bakeoff of *bets* — discover the substrates in the
   slice versus decide them first — not of models. The result will say more
   about the bets than about the leads, and §3 is written so that it can.
2. **The name is Snapback 4.** Siblings, not a sequence: "4" does not mean
   "after 3." A separate number gives the track its own corpus root,
   directory, package identity and data directory with no rename when the
   bakeoff resolves, and files never move in LLP. If Snapback 4 loses, it is
   a number that never shipped. "Snapback 3b" was considered and rejected:
   it reads as a variant of 3, and this is a different bet.
3. **Snapback 4 builds LLP 2000.000 as written.** Its §14 open questions are
   the lead's to decide inside the track, recorded in §7 as they are
   decided. The author rules on the bar, the comparison and promotion (§3).
4. **One owner on the core.** The lead writes the engine, the store and the
   client contract. Codex lanes build the fixture generator, the reference
   applications, the device witnesses and the periphery. Blind reviews from
   two model families are reserved for the two disclosure-sensitive
   mechanisms: partition inversion of read rules (LLP 2000.000 §7.1) and
   the meter's cut behaviour on non-uniform scans (LLP 2000.000 §6). This
   departs from the standing rule that Codex codes and Claude orchestrates,
   deliberately, for the core only.
5. **The clock is four weeks** from the first commit under `snapback4/` to
   the first slice running on the hub fixture. At the clock the author kills
   the track, merges its substrates into a survivor, or continues it. There
   is no third month without a ruling.
6. **Shared and not shared.** Shared with Snapback 3: the LLP corpus, the
   Clique harness and scorers, the fixtures, the briefs, and the simulator
   once either track has one. Not shared: code, except the Snapback 2 pieces
   both are expected to copy (LLP 2000.000 §5.1).
7. **Snapback 2 keeps shipping and freezes new substrate work for the
   duration.** Fix-forward, the loop bar, acquisition and papercuts continue;
   no new certificate axes, client custody mechanisms or ceiling changes.
   This is accepted here as a condition of the bakeoff. Making it binding on
   concurrent Snapback 2 sessions needs one line in `rules/NOT-DOING.md`'s
   Moves ledger, which this document does not write.
8. **Reading load.** This root, updated in place, and one append-only
   journal, `snapback4/JOURNAL.md`. Sub-LLPs only for a decision that must
   outlive the journal. No panels beyond decision 4's two reviews.

## 2. The bet on one page

**Keep verbatim from Snapback 2** (LLP 2000.000 §5.1): the rule language
with its uniformity and hoist analysis, `decided_true` and the
structural-fact refusals; one data language, Quarry, with `--` comments,
`require … else CODE`, `shape`, `merge`, `walk`, `chunk`; the value model
and its conformance corpus; typed read and write states with no silent state
and the refusal envelope `{code, family, site, message, rewrite, guide}`; the
successor classifier (widening additive, checked narrowing, exact projection
ownership); `deliver`'s engine-computed audience, tombstones and
`bootstrap`; `schedule`, `job`, `chunk` and rehearsal; personas; `init`,
`dev`, `check`, `doctor`, `run`, `test`, `why`, `trace`, `guide`; H0
`deploy`, `rollback`, `secret`; channels; assets; the word-prefix index.

**Flip 1 — certify authorization, meter resources** (LLP 2000.000 §6). The
certificate keeps every read site's shape, uniformity, completeness class
and prediction eligibility, and stops pricing bytes and steps. A
deterministic meter charges examined rows, index entries, rule probes,
steps, heap, output and rows written as the program runs, on the server and
in the client interpreter alike. A query cut by the meter returns `capped`
with no continuation past the cut, the same observable outcome as a static
ceiling cut today; a mutation aborts with `E_BOUND` naming actual work; a
job is chunked. `check --cost` prints the structural cost class; `test`
prints measured meters on the hub fixture.

**Flip 2 — the viewer's partition is the unit of sync** (LLP 2000.000 §7).
`sync to <audience> last N by <index>` on a table makes the engine maintain,
per principal, the rows that principal may read, as a change log with a
horizon; a table without the word is online-only, and `check` says which
rule term prevented inversion. The client holds a replica of its partitions,
one watermark each, a durable outbox with client-minted ids, and the
interpreter; queries run locally and are `complete` inside the horizon.
Revocation is a scope tombstone; `until-revoked` and `delivered-history`
survive as the client's leave policy. Two client tiers — online-only

# LLP 2000.000: Snapback 3 — keep the core, flip two substrates, start at hub scale

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Draft
**Role:** Second opinion on LLP 2000; since 2026-09-12 also the design brief Snapback 4 builds (LLP 3000)
**Systems:** Snapback 3 product architecture, bounded computation, client data model, client API vocabulary, language and tooling, effects runtime, verification (simulation), performance budgets, process
**Author:** Claude Fable 5.1, at Charlie Cheever's request
**Date:** 2026-09-12
**Revised:** 2026-09-12 (adopted as the Snapback 4 design brief by LLP 3000 decision 3); 2026-09-12 (initial)
**Related:** [LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md) (parent), [LLP 3000](./3000-snapback4.explainer.md) (the Snapback 4 root that builds this brief), LLP 0000, [LLP 0329](./0329-agent-native-rebuild-diagnosis.research.md), [LLP 0329.014.004](./0329.014.004-bounded-data-programs-v1-design.rfc.md), [LLP 0329.016](./0329.016-agentic-dev-loop-from-scratch.rfc.md), [LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md), [LLP 1001](./1001-query-engine.spec.md), [LLP 1002](./1002-dev-loop.spec.md), [LLP 1012](./1012-local-first-v1.spec.md), [LLP 1018.003](./1018.003-truthful-and-composed-client.decision.md), [LLP 1018.008](./1018.008-elegance-after-the-corrections.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.007](./1018.008.007-affordable-offline-acquisition.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.008](./1018.008.008-locality-of-application-changes.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.009](./1018.008.009-residual-ergonomic-gaps.research.md), [LLP 1019](./1019-derived-delivery-custody.rfc.md), [LLP 1020](./1020-day-two-evolution-and-legible-ceilings.rfc.md), [LLP 1023](./1023-clique-builder-jump.rfc.md), [LLP 1024](./1024-single-lane-delivered-search.rfc.md), [LLP 1025](./1025-digest-final-emission-at-hub-scale.research.md), `rules/RULES.md`, `rules/NOT-DOING.md`, `benchmarks/runs/2026-09-05-clique-full-3x3/holistic-scores.md`

## 1. Summary

LLP 2000 is right that the whole application is the unit of design, right
that ownership comes before abstraction, and right to ask for deterministic
simulation and an early real deployment. Its weakness is that it treats the
two structural choices that produced Snapback 2's costs as open research
questions, and then proposes a first experiment at exactly the scale where
those costs are invisible. This document takes a position on both, names
what to keep from Snapback 2 verbatim, and rewrites the first slice so it
can fail for the right reasons.

The position, in one paragraph. Snapback 2's *core* is excellent and should
be copied: the rule language and its uniformity analysis, the structural-fact
family, one data language, typed states with no silence, refusals that paste
a rewrite, personas, the successor classifier, the derived per-recipient
log, the loop verbs and their sub-second budgets. Two *substrates* under
that core are where the record shows the hours went, and both should be
flipped rather than re-investigated: (1) the static certificate should keep
certifying **authorization and shape** and stop pricing **bytes and steps**,
which move to a deterministic runtime meter with honest `capped`/abort
outcomes; and (2) the client should hold **a replica of the viewer's declared
partition** — the local-first shape every shipped sync engine and Snapback
2's own `deliver` log converge on — instead of a per-query result cache
proven by receipts. Those two flips dissolve most of the machinery that
leaked into the application (receipts, coverage, halos, validators, grants,
ID slices, drains, `withHistory`, follower inboxes, per-table retention
words) and turn the 28-second acquisition into a bulk stream whose floor is
the device's write speed. The first slice should be built on the **hub
fixture** (1,000 memberships, 500 follows, 100,000 messages), with the
day-two change designed before the day-one screen, a native client in the
first slice, and a deterministic simulator as the primary test harness.

Three claims this document makes that LLP 2000 does not:

1. **The costs have two named causes, and both are decisions, not
   mysteries.** Byte-priced static certification and the receipt-proven
   result cache account for every ergonomic residual in LLP 1018.008.009
   except documentation. §2 shows the mapping.
2. **The first experiment must include the hub.** Snapback 2 was "elegant on
   day one and hostile on day two" (LLP 1020) and broke at 1,000 memberships
   (LLPs 1023, 1024, 1025). A two-principal slice will pass and teach nothing.
3. **The process is part of the product.** Seventy-one LLPs, over two
   thousand commits, and seven ceiling raises in fourteen days produced a
   sound system nobody can hold in their head. Snapback 3 needs one owner on
   the core, a simulator instead of a test matrix, and budgets anchored to
   competitors so that raising one means admitting a loss.

## 2. What the record says, read as causes

The evidence LLP 2000 §2 cites is right; its reading is too gentle. Every
row below is a Snapback 2 cost recorded in the corpus, with the substrate
that produced it. Numbers are the corpus's own and retain its scope limits.

| Recorded cost | Where | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding `editedAt: time ?` (44 bytes × 244 retained copies = 10,736) pushed `messages.searchAll` to 4,199,688 closure bytes against 4,194,304; the builder shrank a page from 20 to 19 | LLP 1018.008.008; 0.0.21 day-two diary | **Static byte pricing.** Closure bytes are a bound on what a receipt could ship; the product paid for the bound, not the work |
| The 1,000-membership digest fold certifies at 9,922,698 heap and 8,691,704 closure bytes and is refused; the recipient-keyed form is admitted at 2,733,253 / 1,848,418 | LLP 1025 §3 | **Static byte pricing** (heap = steps × 32 + closure scratch). A runtime meter would have run the fold and reported actual bytes |
| A message page is 50, not 200, because a row "prices at 16,016 bytes" and 200 exceed the 1 MiB output ceiling | LLP 1012 §3 | **Static byte pricing** of the worst-case row width |

Against that, what scored: on the 2026-09-05 three-scorer Clique run
Snapback 2 beat Convex on authorization (82 vs 79) and offline (81 vs 44)
and lost on queries and live (60 vs 85), client integration (59 vs 79),
setup and docs (55 vs 79), diagnostics and loop (66 vs 77), operations (53
vs 76) and scale (62 vs 80); overall 66 vs 81. The later single-lane 0.0.21
and 0.0.25 scores of 82 and 85 are real improvement and not a three-scorer
comparison. The wins are the core; the losses are composition, discovery,
scale and operations — the substrates and what sits on them.

LLP 2000 §2 summarises this as "costs arise where one layer must reconstruct
another layer's facts." True, and the layer doing the reconstructing is the
client, because it was designed as a cache that may not compute. Name the
cause and the remedy follows.

## 3. Where LLP 2000 is right, and should not be diluted

- **The whole application is the unit.** §3's four properties (composition,
  locality, continuity, performance) are the right acceptance vocabulary.
  Keep them as the headings of the scenario suite.
- **Ownership before abstraction.** §5's table is the best paragraph in the
  document. §8 below turns its fourth row into a fixed vocabulary.
- **Composed reads must not fabricate.** Unknown totals stay unknown; revoked
  rows do not linger. Both flips below preserve this; they change what is
  *known*, not what is *claimed*.
- **Writes have one lifecycle with durable admission distinct from commit
  and stable operation identity.** Keep LLP 1018.004's three outcomes.
- **Rust and SQLite.** Yes, and the engine's transaction, interpreter, rule
  evaluation and successor logic are the pieces to copy first (§5).
- **Prototype the experience before the core.** Yes — and §8 makes the
  prototype's API signatures binding on the implementation, not the reverse.

fn bound_role(bound:&Bound,catalog:&Catalog,info:&super::super::catalog::TableInfo,expr:&Expr,recipient:&str)->Option<RuleExpr>{
    let Expr::Exists{read,..}=expr else{return None;};
    // Bind a positive recipient probe after substituting only its principal.
    if !read.keys.iter().any(|k|matches!(&k.value,Expr::Name{name,..} if name==recipient)){return None;}
    let mut value=expr.clone();super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value,&mut |e|if let Expr::Name{name,site}=e{
        if name=="viewer"{*e=Expr::Literal{value:ast::Literal::Str("service:security-assigner-marker".into()),site:site.clone()};}
        else if name==recipient{*name="viewer".into();}
    });
    let rule=super::super::schema::bind_rule(catalog,info,&ast::RuleDecl{effect:ast::Effect::Read,bindings:Vec::new(),site:expr.site().clone(),value}).ok()?;
    let RuleExpr::Exists{table,index,key,equalities,..}=&rule else{return None;};
    let principal=super::privilege::global_principal(bound,table)?;
    let pairs=super::privilege::probe_pairs(bound,table,index,key,equalities);
    if !pairs.iter().any(|(c,v)|c==&principal&&*v==RuleTerm::Viewer){return None;}
    let roles=super::privilege::role_columns(bound,table);
    let equalities=pairs.into_iter().filter(|(c,v)|roles.contains(c)&&matches!(v,RuleTerm::Literal(snapback4_core::Value::String(_)))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if equalities.is_empty(){return None;}
    let index=bound.schema.tables[table].indexes.iter().find(|(_,i)|i.unique&&i.columns()==vec![principal.clone()])?.0.clone();
    Some(RuleExpr::Exists{table:table.clone(),index,key:vec![RuleTerm::Viewer],equalities,provenance:snapback4_core::ir::KeyProvenance::Computed})

}

fn same_target(base:&Expr,w:&Write<'_>)->bool{match base{
    Expr::Assert{value,..}=>same_target(value,w),
    Expr::Read(read)=>read.table==w.table&&read.keys.len()==w.keys.len()&&read.keys.iter().zip(&w.keys).all(|(a,b)|a.column==b.column&&crate::print::expression(&a.value)==crate::print::expression(&b.value)),
    _=>false,
}}
fn positive_probes(rule:&RuleExpr)->Vec<&RuleExpr>{match rule{RuleExpr::And(xs)=>xs.iter().flat_map(positive_probes).collect(),RuleExpr::Exists{..}=>vec![rule],_=>vec![]}}
fn transition_notes(bound:&Bound,_catalog:&Catalog,writes:&[Write<'_>],out:&mut Vec<Diagnostic>){
    for w in writes{let t=&bound.schema.tables[&w.table];
        if w.op==WriteOp::Update{for f in &w.fields{
            let Some(ColumnType::Enum{..})=t.columns.get(&f.name).map(ColumnType::required)else{continue;};
            let Some(Expr::Name{name,..})=field_value(f)else{continue;};
            let Some(arg)=w.p.args.iter().find(|a|a.name==*name)else{continue;};let TypeKind::Enum{variants}=&arg.type_.kind else{continue;};
            for other in writes.iter().filter(|o|o.op==WriteOp::Update&&o.table==w.table&&o.p.name!=w.p.name){
                let mut targets=BTreeSet::new();for g in other.fields.iter().filter(|g|g.name==f.name){if let Some(value)=field_value(g){walk(value,|e|if let Expr::Literal{value:ast::Literal::Str(v),..}=e{targets.insert(v.clone());});}}
                for target in &targets{
                    if variants.contains(target)&&!conditions(&w.context).iter().any(|e|super::lints::argument_guard(e,name,target)==Some(false))&&kernel::implies(&w.gate,&other.gate)==Ok(false){note(out,&w.site,"N_TRANSITION_BYPASS",format!("{}: generic {}.{} setter includes '{target}', also set by stricter {} ({})",w.p.name,w.table,f.name,other.p.name,other.gate.quarry()),"enforce the decision's authority on every path reaching this status; declare independent transition/column update intent and run test");}
                }
            }
        }}
        if !matches!(w.op,WriteOp::Insert|WriteOp::Upsert){continue;}
        let deps=conditions(&w.context).iter().flat_map(|e|reads(e)).filter(|dep|dep!=&w.table&&super::privilege::role_columns(bound,dep).is_empty()&&writes.iter().any(|o|&o.table==dep&&o.op!=WriteOp::Insert)).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        for dep in deps{for later in writes.iter().filter(|o|o.p.name!=w.p.name&&(o.table==w.table&&o.op==WriteOp::Update||bound.schema.tables[&o.table].columns.values().any(|k|matches!(k.required(),ColumnType::Ref{table} if table==&w.table)))){
            if conditions(&later.context).iter().any(|e|reads(e).contains(&dep)){continue;}
            note(out,&later.site,"N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK",format!("{}: {} creation by {} checks mutable {dep}, but this later {} write does not recheck it",later.p.name,w.table,w.p.name,later.table),"if eligibility must remain current at approval/transition, recheck it there; declare independent intent and test a create -> eligibility change -> approval history");
        }}
    }
}

fn duration_number(e:&Expr)->Option<i64>{
    let Expr::Literal{value:ast::Literal::Number(s),..}=e else{return None;};
    for (suffix,scale) in [("ms",1),("s",1000),("m",60_000),("h",3_600_000),("d",86_400_000)]{
        if let Some(n)=s.strip_suffix(suffix){return n.parse::<i64>().ok()?.checked_mul(scale);}
    }s.parse().ok()
}
fn duration_notes(writes:&[Write<'_>],out:&mut Vec<Diagnostic>){
    let mut bounds=BTreeMap::<(String,String,String),BTreeMap<i64,BTreeSet<String>>>::new();
    let mut sites=BTreeMap::new();
    for w in writes{for condition in conditions(&w.context){walk(condition,|e|{
        let Expr::Binary{op,left,right,..}=e else{return;};if !matches!(op.as_str(),">"|">="|"<"|"<="){return;}
        for (field,clock,cmp) in [(left.as_ref(),right.as_ref(),op.as_str()),(right.as_ref(),left.as_ref(),match op.as_str(){">"=>"<",">="=>"<=","<"=>">",_=>">="})]{
            let Expr::Binary{op:offset,left:now,right:amount,..}=clock else{continue;};
            if !matches!(now.as_ref(),Expr::Name{name,..} if name=="now")||!matches!(offset.as_str(),"-"|"+"){continue;}
            let Some(mut duration)=duration_number(amount)else{continue;};if offset=="-"{duration=-duration;}
            let target=match field{
                Expr::Member{base,name,..}=>reads(base).into_iter().next().map(|table|(table,name.clone())),
                Expr::Name{name,..}=>writes.iter().filter(|a|a.p.name==w.p.name).find_map(|a|a.fields.iter().find(|f|field_value(f).is_some_and(|e|matches!(e,Expr::Name{name:n,..} if n==name))).map(|f|(a.table.clone(),f.name.clone()))),_=>None,
            };
            if let Some((table,column))=target{let key=(table,column,cmp.to_string());sites.entry(key.clone()).or_insert_with(||w.site.clone());bounds.entry(key).or_default().entry(duration).or_default().insert(w.p.name.clone());}
        }
    });}}
    for ((table,column,cmp),values) in bounds{if values.len()<2{continue;}
        let entries=values.iter().map(|(ms,ops)|format!("now {ms:+}ms in {}",ops.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ");
        note(out,&sites[&(table.clone(),column.clone(),cmp.clone())],"N_DURATION_BOUNDS",format!("{table}.{column}: inconsistent `{cmp}` duration bounds across operations: {entries}; are these different windows intentional?"),"use the specification's duration consistently at creation, renewal and approval, or document the deliberate workflow difference");
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#151-every-executed-write — conditional advice never infers creation policy.
use super::*;
pub(super) fn notes(sources:&[(String,String)],bound:&Bound)->Vec<Diagnostic>{

    let catalog=Catalog::build(documents.clone(),&mut Vec::new());
    let mut writes=Vec::new();
    for doc in &documents{for p in &doc.programs{if p.kind!=ast::ProgramKind::Mutation{continue;}
        for (write,context) in super::authority_walk::writes(&catalog,p){
            let ast::Expr::Write{op,table,fields,site,..}=write else{continue;};
            let Some(info)=catalog.tables.get(&table)else{continue;};
            let requirements=super::operation::requirements(&catalog,info,&context);
            let t=&bound.schema.tables[&table];
            let gate=if op==ast::WriteOp::Update{t.update_rule_judged().into_owned()}else{t.rules.insert.clone()};
            let admission=RuleExpr::And(requirements.into_iter().chain([gate]).collect());
            writes.push((p.name.clone(),op,table,fields,site,admission));
        }
    }}
    fn necessary(rule:&RuleExpr)->RuleExpr{match rule{
        RuleExpr::And(xs)=>RuleExpr::And(xs.iter().map(necessary).collect()),
        _ if super::operation::safe(rule)=>rule.clone(),_=>RuleExpr::Allow,
    }}
    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut seen=BTreeSet::new();
    for (name,op,table,fields,site,admission) in &writes{
        if !matches!(op,ast::WriteOp::Insert|ast::WriteOp::Upsert){continue;}
        for (editor,edit,other,patch,_,restricted) in &writes{
            if *edit!=ast::WriteOp::Update||other!=table{continue;}
            let restriction=necessary(restricted);
            if kernel::implies(&RuleExpr::Allow,&restriction)==Ok(true)||kernel::implies(admission,&restriction)!=Ok(false){continue;}
            let columns=patch.iter().filter(|f|fields.iter().any(|insert|{
                if insert.name!=f.name{return false;}
                let Some(value)=&insert.value else{return true;};
                let mut value=value.clone();let mut supplied=false;
                super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value,&mut |e|if let ast::Expr::Name{name:argument,..}=e{
                    supplied|=documents.iter().flat_map(|d|&d.programs).filter(|p|p.name==*name).any(|p|p.args.iter().any(|a|a.name==*argument));
                });supplied
            })).map(|f|f.name.clone()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
            if columns.is_empty()||!seen.insert((name.clone(),table.clone(),columns.clone(),restriction.quarry())){continue;}
            out.push(Diagnostic::new(site,"N_INSERT_WRITE_INTENT",format!("{name}: {table}.{} can be supplied at insert/upsert without the edit restriction of {editor}: {}; creation admission: {}",columns.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(","),restriction.quarry(),admission.quarry()),"confirm whether the spec permits different creation authority; otherwise guard every insert/upsert arm too and declare column write only intent, then run snapback4 test").guide("security"));
        }
    }out
}

//! Expand advisory write sites with lexical arguments and dominating guards.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#128-runtime-intent-and-independent-worlds — helper placement cannot hide a grant writer.
use super::*;
use ast::{Expr,Stmt,ProgramDecl,FunctionBody};
type Env=BTreeMap<String,Expr>;
fn resolve(expr:&Expr,env:&Env)->Expr{
    let mut expr=expr.clone();
    super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut expr,&mut |e|{
        if let Expr::Object{fields,..}|Expr::Write{fields,..}=e{for f in fields{if f.value.is_none(){f.value=Some(env.get(&f.name).cloned().unwrap_or_else(||Expr::Name{name:f.name.clone(),site:f.site.clone()}));}}}
        if let Expr::Name{name,..}=e&&let Some(value)=env.get(name){*e=value.clone();}
    });expr
}
fn expression(catalog:&Catalog,p:&ProgramDecl,expr:&Expr,env:&Env,guards:&[Stmt],depth:usize,out:&mut Vec<(Expr,ProgramDecl)>){
    let mut expr=resolve(expr,env);
    super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut expr,&mut |e|match e{
        Expr::Write{..}=>{let mut context=p.clone();context.prelude=Vec::new();context.body=guards.to_vec();out.push((e.clone(),context));},
        Expr::Call{name,args,..} if depth<32=>if let Some(f)=catalog.functions.get(name){
            let mut locals=f.args.iter().zip(args).map(|(arg,value)|(arg.name.clone(),value.clone())).collect();
            let mut inherited=guards.to_vec();
            match &f.body{
                FunctionBody::Expression(value)=>expression(catalog,p,value,&locals,&inherited,depth+1,out),
                FunctionBody::Block(body)=>statements(catalog,p,body,&mut locals,&mut inherited,depth+1,out),
            }
        },_=>{}
    });
}
// Only an unconditional direct call exports a helper's guaranteed prefix.
// Conditional/loop-local requirements never become caller assumptions.
fn helper_guards(catalog:&Catalog,expr:&Expr,env:&Env,depth:usize)->Vec<Stmt>{
    if depth>=32{return Vec::new();}
    let Expr::Call{name,args,..}=resolve(expr,env)else{return Vec::new();};
    let Some(f)=catalog.functions.get(&name)else{return Vec::new();};
    let mut locals=f.args.iter().zip(args).map(|(a,v)|(a.name.clone(),v)).collect::<Env>();
    let FunctionBody::Block(body)=&f.body else{return if let FunctionBody::Expression(value)=&f.body{helper_guards(catalog,value,&locals,depth+1)}else{Vec::new()};};
    let mut out=Vec::new();
    for s in body{match s{
        Stmt::Require{condition,code,message,site}=>out.push(Stmt::Require{condition:resolve(condition,&locals),code:code.clone(),message:message.clone(),site:site.clone()}),
        Stmt::Bind{names,value,..}=>{out.extend(helper_guards(catalog,value,&locals,depth+1));if names.len()==1{locals.insert(names[0].clone(),resolve(value,&locals));}},
        Stmt::Expr{value,..}=>out.extend(helper_guards(catalog,value,&locals,depth+1)),
        Stmt::Return{value,..}=>{out.extend(helper_guards(catalog,value,&locals,depth+1));break;},_=>break,
    }}out
}
fn statements(catalog:&Catalog,p:&ProgramDecl,body:&[Stmt],env:&mut Env,guards:&mut Vec<Stmt>,depth:usize,out:&mut Vec<(Expr,ProgramDecl)>){
    for s in body{match s{
        Stmt::Bind{names,value,..}=>{expression(catalog,p,value,env,guards,depth,out);guards.extend(helper_guards(catalog,value,env,0));if names.len()==1{env.insert(names[0].clone(),resolve(value,env));}},
        Stmt::Require{condition,code,message,site}=>{
            expression(catalog,p,condition,env,guards,depth,out);
            guards.push(Stmt::Require{condition:resolve(condition,env),code:code.clone(),message:message.clone(),site:site.clone()});
        },
        Stmt::Return{value,..}=>{expression(catalog,p,value,env,guards,depth,out);break;},
        Stmt::Expr{value,..}=>{expression(catalog,p,value,env,guards,depth,out);guards.extend(helper_guards(catalog,value,env,0));},
        Stmt::If{condition,then_body,else_body,site}=>{
            expression(catalog,p,condition,env,guards,depth,out);
            let condition=resolve(condition,env);
            let mut then_guards=guards.clone();
            then_guards.push(Stmt::Require{condition:condition.clone(),code:"$advice".into(),message:None,site:site.clone()});
            statements(catalog,p,then_body,&mut env.clone(),&mut then_guards,depth,out);
            let mut else_guards=guards.clone();
            else_guards.push(Stmt::Require{condition:Expr::Unary{op:"not".into(),value:Box::new(condition),site:site.clone()},code:"$advice".into(),message:None,site:site.clone()});
            statements(catalog,p,else_body,&mut env.clone(),&mut else_guards,depth,out);
        },
        Stmt::For{domain,name,body,..}=>{expression(catalog,p,domain,env,guards,depth,out);let mut local=env.clone();local.remove(name);statements(catalog,p,body,&mut local,&mut guards.clone(),depth,out);},
        Stmt::As{body,..}=>statements(catalog,p,body,&mut env.clone(),&mut guards.clone(),depth,out),_=>{}
    }}
}
pub(super) fn writes(catalog:&Catalog,p:&ProgramDecl)->Vec<(Expr,ProgramDecl)>{
    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut env=Env::new();let mut guards=Vec::new();
    statements(catalog,p,&p.prelude,&mut env,&mut guards,0,&mut out);
    statements(catalog,p,&p.body,&mut env,&mut guards,0,&mut out);out
}
//! Narrow stable leading-require reduction for operation-specific authority.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#81-exact-conservative-boundary-review-clarification — unknown write sets never establish stability.
use super::*;
use crate::ast::{Stmt,ProgramDecl,ProgramKind,InvariantDecl,RuleDecl};
use super::super::catalog::TableInfo;
pub(super) fn resolve<'a>(catalog:&'a Catalog,decl:&InvariantDecl)->Option<(String,&'a ProgramDecl)>{
    if matches!(decl.target.as_str(),"read"|"insert"|"update"|"delete"|"always"|"write"){return None;}
    let matches=catalog.documents.iter().flat_map(|d|{let module=std::path::Path::new(&d.file).file_stem().unwrap().to_string_lossy();d.programs.iter().map(move|p|(super::super::operation_name(&module,&p.name),p))})
        .filter(|(name,p)|p.kind==ProgramKind::Mutation&&(name==&decl.target||p.name==decl.target)).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if matches.len()==1 {matches.into_iter().next()}else{None}
}
pub(super) fn safe(rule:&RuleExpr)->bool {match rule{
    RuleExpr::Exists{key,equalities,..}=>key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_,t)|t)).all(|t|matches!(t,RuleTerm::Viewer|RuleTerm::Literal(_))),
    RuleExpr::And(xs)|RuleExpr::Or(xs)=>xs.iter().all(safe),
    RuleExpr::Eq(a,b)|RuleExpr::Ne(a,b)=>[a,b].iter().all(|t|matches!(t,RuleTerm::Viewer|RuleTerm::Literal(_))),
    RuleExpr::Allow|RuleExpr::Deny|RuleExpr::Public{..}=>true,_=>false,
}}
pub(super) fn requirements(catalog:&Catalog,info:&TableInfo,p:&ProgramDecl)->Vec<RuleExpr>{
    let mut out=Vec::new();
    for s in p.prelude.iter().chain(&p.body){let Stmt::Require{condition,site,..}=s else{break};
        let decl=RuleDecl{effect:ast::Effect::Read,bindings:Vec::new(),value:condition.clone(),site:site.clone()};
        if let Ok(rule)=super::super::schema::bind_rule(catalog,info,&decl)&&safe(&rule){out.push(rule);}
    }out
}
pub(super) fn prove(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant)->Result<bool,String>{
    let p=bound.programs.iter().find(|p|Some(&p.program.name)==inv.operation.as_ref()).ok_or("operation did not bind")?;
    if !safe(inv.policy.as_ref().ok_or("unsupported policy")?){return Err("operation policy needs unsupported target-image, negative-probe or live-reference bindings".into());}
    let writes=snapback4_core::ir::write_tables(&p.program);
    if !writes.iter().any(|(t,_)|t==&inv.table){return Err("operation has no direct write to the named table; implicit effects require a reduction".into());}
    let dependencies=inv.requirements.iter().flat_map(kernel::dependencies).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    if writes.iter().any(|(t,_)|dependencies.contains(t)) {return Err("require dependency can be changed by this operation, including its target write".into());}
    if bound.schema.tables.values().any(|t|!t.maintained.is_empty()||!t.sequences.is_empty()||t.on_delete.values().any(|a|a.writes())) || !bound.schema.maintains.is_empty(){return Err("implicit maintain/sequence/referential writes require dependency stability reduction".into());}
    // Source helpers/control flow may hide write sets or viewer changes.
    let json=serde_json::to_value(&p.program).unwrap();
    fn opaque(v:&serde_json::Value)->bool{match v{serde_json::Value::Object(m)=>m.keys().any(|k|matches!(k.as_str(),"For"|"If"|"JobAs"|"JobQuery"|"Emit"))||m.values().any(opaque),serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>xs.iter().any(opaque),_=>false}}
    if opaque(&json){return Err("operation control flow or opaque effects are outside stable leading-require reduction".into());}
    let admission=RuleExpr::And(inv.requirements.clone());
    // Table-rule gates can only further restrict a dominating stable require;
    // using the require alone overapproximates effective owner-field gates.
    kernel::implies(&admission,inv.policy.as_ref().unwrap())
}

pub struct Campaign {pub directed_attempts:usize,pub directed_peak_worlds:usize,#[serde(skip)] pub history_limit:usize,#[serde(skip)] pub generated_fixture:bool,#[serde(skip)] pub work_remaining:Option<usize>,#[serde(skip)] pub deadline:Option<std::time::Instant>,pub paired_observer_calls:usize,pub history_observer_calls:usize,pub column_observer_calls:usize,pub operations:BTreeMap<String,usize>,pub sequences:usize,pub attempted:usize,pub admitted:usize,pub refused:usize,pub violations:Vec<Counterexample>,pub boundary_failures:Vec<String>,pub unsupported:BTreeSet<String>}
impl Campaign {
    pub fn bounded(milliseconds:u64)->Self {Self{work_remaining:Some(512),deadline:Some(std::time::Instant::now()+std::time::Duration::from_millis(milliseconds)),..Self::default()}}
    pub(super) fn reserve(&mut self,cost:usize)->bool {
        if self.exhausted(){return false;}
        if let Some(remaining)=&mut self.work_remaining {
            if *remaining<cost{*remaining=0;self.unsupported.insert("check concrete exploration work budget exhausted; remaining paths unproved; run snapback4 test for the full campaign".into());return false;}
            *remaining-=cost;
        }true
    }
    pub(super) fn exhausted(&mut self)->bool {
        if self.work_remaining==Some(0){self.unsupported.insert("check concrete exploration work budget exhausted; remaining paths unproved; run snapback4 test for the full campaign".into());return true;}
        if self.deadline.is_some_and(|deadline|std::time::Instant::now()>=deadline){self.unsupported.insert("check concrete exploration time budget exhausted; remaining paths unproved; run snapback4 test for the full campaign".into());true}else{false}
    }
}
fn id(table:&str)->Value {Value::Id(format!("security-{table}"))}
fn sample(kind:&C,variant:usize)->Option<Value>{Some(match kind{
    C::Optional(inner)=>if variant&4!=0{sample(inner,variant).unwrap_or(Value::Null)}else{Value::Null},C::Id|C::Principal=>Value::Id(if variant&1==0{VIEWER}else{OTHER}.into()),
    C::Ref{table}=>id(table),C::Text{max}=>Value::String("x".repeat((*max).min(20) as usize)),
    C::Enum{variants}=>Value::String(variants.get(variant%variants.len())?.clone()),
    C::Int|C::Decimal{..}|C::Money{..}=>Value::Int(1),C::IntRange{min,max}=>Value::Int(1i64.clamp(*min,*max)),
    C::Bool=>Value::Bool((variant>>2)&1==0),C::Time=>Value::Int(NOW-1000),C::Json{..}=>Value::Null,C::Bytes{..}=>Value::Bytes(Vec::new()),
    C::List{..}=>Value::Array(Vec::new()),C::ListRange{of,min,..}=>Value::Array((0..*min).map(|_|sample(of,variant)).collect::<Option<_>>()?),
    C::Image{..}=>Value::String("$security:image".into()),C::File{..}=>Value::String("$security:file".into()),C::Video{..}=>return None,
})}
fn needed(schema:&Schema,name:&str,out:&mut BTreeSet<String>){
    if !out.insert(name.into()){return;}let Some(t)=schema.table(name)else{return};
    for m in schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m|m.target==name){needed(schema,&m.source,out);}
    for k in t.columns.values(){if let C::Ref{table}=k.required(){needed(schema,table,out);}}
    for r in super::columns::rules(t){for dep in kernel::dependencies(r){needed(schema,&dep,out);}}
}
fn snapshot(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant,variant:usize)->Result<BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,String>{
    snapshot_mode(bound,inv,variant,false)
}
fn snapshot_mode(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant,variant:usize,timed:bool)->Result<BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,String>{
    let mut names=BTreeSet::new();needed(&bound.schema,&inv.table,&mut names);
    if let Some(policy)=&inv.policy{for dep in kernel::dependencies(policy){needed(&bound.schema,&dep,&mut names);}}
    if let Some(mut syntax)=inv.syntax.clone(){super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut syntax,&mut |e| {
        if let ast::Expr::Read(r)|ast::Expr::Exists{read:r,..}=e {needed(&bound.schema,&r.table,&mut names);}
    });}
    if let Some(op)=&inv.operation && let Some(p)=bound.programs.iter().find(|p|&p.program.name==op){for kind in p.program.args.values(){if let ir::ArgType::Ref{table}=kind{needed(&bound.schema,table,&mut names);}}}
    let mut out=BTreeMap::new();
    let mut enum_case=variant;
    for name in names {
        let t=&bound.schema.tables[&name];
        if bound.schema.maintain_for(&name).is_some(){continue;}
        let mut fields=BTreeMap::new();fields.insert("id".into(),id(&name));
        let mut principal_index=0usize;
        for (n,k) in &t.columns{
            if n=="id"||t.engine_field(n)||t.maintained.contains_key(n){continue;}
            let sample_variant=if let C::Enum{variants}=k.required(){let n=enum_case % variants.len();enum_case/=variants.len();n}else if matches!(k.required(),C::Principal){let n=((variant>>((if name==inv.table{0}else{3})+principal_index.min(5)))&1)|(variant&4);principal_index+=1;n}else{variant};
            let value=sample(k,sample_variant)
                .ok_or_else(||format!("{name}.{n}: asset ledger/required sample is not available"))?;
            fields.insert(n.clone(),value);
        }
        if timed || t.read_lifetime_sensitive() {for (n,k) in &t.columns {if matches!(k.required(),C::Time)&&(!k.is_optional()||variant&4!=0) {
            fields.insert(n.clone(),Value::Int(NOW+if t.expire.as_ref()==Some(n){2000}else if timed{1000}else{-1000}));
        }}}
        for constraint in &t.constraints{if let Constraint::Text{field,min,..}=constraint
            && matches!(fields.get(field),Some(Value::String(_))) {fields.insert(field.clone(),Value::String("x".repeat((*min).max(1) as usize)));}}
        // Named primary keys used by role probes must select the challenged
        // viewer; changing the enum represents a current-role change while
        // derived assignment/membership rows remain present.
        if name!=inv.table {for (i,(n,k)) in t.columns.iter().filter(|(_,k)|matches!(k,C::Principal)).enumerate(){fields.insert(n.clone(),Value::Id(if variant & (1 << (i+3)) == 0 {VIEWER}else{OTHER}.into())); let _=k;}}
        out.insert(name,vec![Value::Row(fields.into())]);
    }
    Ok(out)
}
struct Snapshot<'a>{schema:&'a Schema,rows:&'a BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>}
impl Probe for Snapshot<'_>{
    fn exists(&mut self,table:&str,index:&str,key:&[Value],equalities:&[(String,Value)])->Result<bool,RuntimeError>{
        let t=&self.schema.tables[table];let Some(idx)=t.index(index)else{return Ok(false)};
        if idx.components.len()!=key.len(){return Ok(false);}
        if idx.unique&&idx.components.iter().any(|c|c.column().is_some_and(|n|t.columns.get(n).is_some_and(C::is_optional)))&&key.contains(&Value::Null){return Ok(false);}
        Ok(self.rows.get(table).into_iter().flatten().filter(|r|live(t,r)).any(|r|idx.components.iter().zip(key).all(|(c,v)|c.column().is_some_and(|n|r.field(n).ok()==Some(v)))&&equalities.iter().all(|(n,v)|r.field(n).ok()==Some(v))))
    }
    fn created(&mut self,_:&str,_:&str,_:&[Value])->bool{false}

}
fn live(t:&snapback4_core::schema::Table,row:&Value)->bool{
    !t.expired(row,NOW)&&t.not_before.as_ref().is_none_or(|c|match row.field(c){Ok(Value::Int(n))=>*n<=NOW,Ok(Value::Null)=>true,_=>false})
}
fn policy(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,viewer:&str,old:Option<&Value>,row:&Value)->Result<bool,String>{

    let Some(p)=inv.policy.as_ref() else{return inv.syntax.as_ref().and_then(|e|super::concrete::evaluate(e,row,rows,&bound.schema,viewer)).ok_or_else(||"concrete policy expression is unknown/unsupported (including clock and typed literal coercions)".into());};

    let mut image=row.clone();if super::temporal::has_clock(p)&&let Value::Row(fields)=&mut image{fields.insert("$security:server-clock".into(),Value::Int(NOW));}
    if p.has_reference(){return Err("reference intent requires authorized engine policy replay".into());}
    rules::evaluate(p,viewer,old,&image,false,&mut Snapshot{schema:&bound.schema,rows}).map_err(|e|e.to_string())
}
fn policy_in(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,viewer:&str,old:Option<&Value>,row:&Value,engine:&mut Engine)->Result<bool,String>{
    let Some(p)=&inv.policy else{return policy(bound,inv,rows,viewer,old,row);};
    if !p.has_reference(){return policy(bound,inv,rows,viewer,old,row);}
    let mut image=row.clone();if super::temporal::has_clock(p)&&let Value::Row(fields)=&mut image{fields.insert("$security:server-clock".into(),Value::Int(NOW));}
    match engine.fixture_policy(p,viewer,old,&image,NOW).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?{
        rules::Verdict::Readable=>Ok(true),rules::Verdict::Denied=>Ok(false),rules::Verdict::Unknown=>Err("policy reference/coverage judgment is unknown; never a refutation".into()),
    }
}
