    engine_with(bound,rows,vec![probe])
}
fn engine_with(bound:&Bound,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,probes:Vec<Program>)->Result<Engine,String>{
    engine_on_store(bound,rows,probes,Store::memory().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?)
}
fn hydrate(engine:&mut Engine,kind:&C,value:&Value)->Result<Value,String>{
        match (kind,value) {
            (C::Optional(inner),v) if *v!=Value::Null=>hydrate(engine,inner,v),
            (C::List{of,..}|C::ListRange{of,..},Value::Array(xs))=>xs.iter().map(|v|hydrate(engine,of,v)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>().map(Value::Array),
            (C::Image{..},Value::String(marker)) if marker=="$security:image"=>engine.store_asset(VIEWER,&PNG,NOW).map(|a|a.column_value()).map_err(|e|format!("verified image fixture: {e}")),
            (C::File{types,..},Value::String(marker)) if marker=="$security:file"=>assets::file(engine,VIEWER,types),
            _=>Ok(value.clone()),
        }
    }

fn engine_on_store(bound:&Bound,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,probes:Vec<Program>,store:impl Into<snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore>)->Result<Engine,String>{
    let mut programs=bound.programs.iter().map(|p|p.program.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>();programs.extend(probes);
    let mut engine=Engine::new_at(store,bound.schema.clone(),programs,NOW).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    let mut seeded=rows.iter().filter(|(name,_)|bound.schema.maintain_for(name).is_none()).map(|(name,rs)|{
        let t=&bound.schema.tables[name];
        let clean=rs.iter().map(|r|if let Value::Row(fields)=r {Value::Row(fields.iter().filter(|(c,_)|!t.engine_field(c)&&!t.recorded.contains_key(*c)&&!t.maintained.contains_key(*c)).map(|(c,v)|(c.clone(),v.clone())).collect())}else{r.clone()}).collect();
        (name.clone(),clean)
    }).collect::<BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>>();
    for (table,values) in &mut seeded {for row in values {for (column,kind) in &bound.schema.tables[table].columns {
        if let Ok(v)=row.field(column) {
            let value=hydrate(&mut engine,kind,v)?;
            if let Value::Row(fields)=row {fields.insert(column.clone(),value);}
        }
    }}}
    engine.seed_at(seeded.iter().flat_map(|(t,rs)|rs.iter().map(move|r|(t.clone(),r.clone()))).collect::<Vec<_>>(),NOW).map_err(|e|format!("generated snapshot rejected by schema: {e}"))?;
    validate_fixture(bound,&mut engine)?;
    Ok(engine)
}
fn validate_fixture(bound:&Bound,engine:&mut Engine)->Result<(),String>{
    let actual=readback(engine)?;
    for (name,values) in &actual {for row in values {
        snapback4_core::engine::validate::validate_row(&bound.schema,name,row).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        for c in &bound.schema.tables[name].constraints {if let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert{table,index,key}=c {
            let rule=RuleExpr::Exists{table:table.clone(),index:index.clone(),key:key.clone(),provenance:KeyProvenance::Computed,equalities:Vec::new()};
            if engine.fixture_policy(&rule,snapback4_core::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL,None,row,NOW).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?!=rules::Verdict::Readable {return Err(format!("{name}: trusted seed did not establish final-exists constraint"));}
        }}
    }}
    Ok(())
}

fn replay(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,viewer:&str,word:&str,row:&Value)->Result<(bool,Value),String>{
    let name="$security.probe";let table=inv.table.clone();let key=id(&table);
    let read=Read{site:"security challenge".into(),table:table.clone(),index:"byId".into(),key:vec![Expr::Literal(key.clone())],provenance:KeyProvenance::Computed};
    let mut seeds=rows.clone();
    let probe=match word{
        "read"=>program(name,ProgramKind::Query,vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Get(read))]),
        "insert"=>{seeds.remove(&table);program(name,ProgramKind::Mutation,vec![Stmt::Insert{table,row:Expr::Literal(row.clone())},Stmt::Return(Expr::Literal(Value::Null))])},
        "delete"=>program(name,ProgramKind::Mutation,vec![Stmt::Delete{table,key:Expr::Literal(key)},Stmt::Return(Expr::Literal(Value::Null))]),
        "update"=>{
            let definition=&bound.schema.tables[&table];
            let changed=definition.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|n.as_str()!="id"&&!definition.engine_field(n))
                .filter(|(n,_)|inv.column.as_ref().is_none_or(|c|c==*n))
                .filter(|(n,_)|!definition.constraints.iter().any(|c|matches!(c,Constraint::Immutable{fields} if fields.contains(n))))
                .find_map(|(n,k)| {let old=row.field(n).ok()?;let next=match (k.required(),old){
                    (C::Bool,Value::Bool(v))=>Value::Bool(!v),
                    (C::Enum{variants},_)=>Value::String(variants.iter().find(|v|Some(Value::String((*v).clone()))!=Some(old.clone()))?.clone()),
                    (C::Text{max},Value::String(v)) if v.chars().count()<*max as usize=>Value::String(format!("{v}x")),
                    (C::Int|C::Time,Value::Int(v))=>Value::Int(v+1),_=>return None};
                    Some((n.clone(),next))});
            let Some((column,value))=changed else{return Err("no valid changed mutable-column sample".into());};
            program(name,ProgramKind::Mutation,vec![Stmt::Update{table,key:Expr::Literal(key),patch:Expr::Literal(Value::Map([(column,value)].into_iter().collect()))},Stmt::Return(Expr::Literal(Value::Null))])
        },_=>return Err("row integrity/transition challenge is not an operation admission test".into()),
    };
    let mut engine=engine(bound,&seeds,probe)?;
    if word=="read"{return engine.query(name,Context::new(viewer,BTreeMap::new()).at(NOW)).map(|q|(q.data!=Value::Null,row.clone())).map_err(|e|e.to_string());}
    let outcome=engine.mutate(name,None,Context::new(viewer,BTreeMap::new()).at(NOW)).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    if !matches!(outcome.state,snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent{..}){return Ok((false,row.clone()));}
    let next=engine.store().rows(&inv.table).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.into_iter().find(|r|r.field("id").ok()==row.field("id").ok());
    if word=="delete"{return if next.is_none(){Ok((true,row.clone()))}else{Err("delete returned sent without removing the target".into())};}
    let next=next.ok_or("sent write has no committed target image")?;
    if word=="update" {
        let table=&bound.schema.tables[&inv.table];
        let changed=table.columns.keys().filter(|c|!table.engine_field(c)&&!table.maintained.contains_key(*c))
            .any(|c|row.field(c).ok()!=next.field(c).ok()&&inv.column.as_ref().is_none_or(|column|column==c));
        if !changed{return Err("sent no-op/implicit-only update has no changed declared target column".into());}
    }
    Ok((true,next))
}
fn readback(engine:&Engine)->Result<BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,String>{engine.schema().tables.keys().map(|t|engine.store().rows(t).map(|rs|(t.clone(),rs)).map_err(|e|e.to_string())).collect()}

fn operation_preflight(bound:&Bound,inv:&Invariant)->Result<(),String>{
    let Some(name)=&inv.operation else{return Ok(());};
    let p=&bound.programs.iter().find(|p|&p.program.name==name).ok_or("operation did not bind")?.program;
    if !super::census::body(&p.body){return Err(format!("{name}: opaque/loop/scan path requires write-boundary tracing"));}
    let rule=inv.policy.as_ref().ok_or("operation policy outside rule fragment")?;
    if rule.any_term(&|t|!matches!(t,RuleTerm::Viewer|RuleTerm::Literal(_))){return Err("operation policy requires write-boundary row-image tracing".into());}
    let writes=ir::write_tables(p);
    if writes.iter().filter(|(t,_)|t==&inv.table).count()>1{return Err(format!("{name}: multiple target writes need executed-effect tracing; net images do not identify delete/reinsert"));}
    let unstable=kernel::dependencies(rule).iter().any(|dep|{
        let hits=writes.iter().filter(|(t,_)|t==dep).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        !hits.is_empty()&&!(dep==&inv.table&&hits.len()==1&&hits[0].1=="insert")
    });
    if unstable||!bound.schema.maintains.is_empty()||bound.schema.tables.values().any(|t|!t.sequences.is_empty()||!t.maintained.is_empty()||t.on_delete.values().any(|a|a.writes())){
        return Err("operation policy dependency may change before/after its write boundary; snapshot correspondence unproved".into());
    }Ok(())
}

/// Schema-only engine challenges. Successful synthetic operations refute the
/// declared table-authority contract, not application-operation reachability.
pub fn run(bound:&Bound)->Campaign{run_selected(bound,None)}
/// `check` searches unproved direct obligations; unsearched blockers remain
/// explicitly unproved. Default `test` passes None and runs the whole set.
pub fn run_selected(bound:&Bound,sites:Option<&BTreeSet<String>>)->Campaign{run_selected_after(bound,sites,Campaign::default())}
/// Continue after trusted observations, preserving one set of work budgets.
pub fn run_selected_after(bound:&Bound,sites:Option<&BTreeSet<String>>,mut out:Campaign)->Campaign{
    // A direct component theorem needs no repeated concrete search for that
    // same component. Indirect observers, temporal reads and actual authored
    // operations below still run; the whole declaration remains unproved.
    let discharged=super::analyze_rules(bound).invariants.into_iter()
        .filter(|v|v.direct_rule==Status::Proved&&v.invariant.operation.is_none()
            && (matches!(v.invariant.target.as_str(),"read"|"always"|"insert"|"delete")
                || matches!(v.invariant.target.as_str(),"update"|"write")&&bound.schema.tables[&v.invariant.table].written_by.is_empty()))
        .map(|v|v.invariant.site.to_string()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    let mut assertions=bound.invariants.clone();
    for inv in &bound.invariants {
        if inv.target=="read"&&inv.column.as_deref().is_some_and(|c|c!="id"){continue;}
        if inv.operation.is_some()||matches!(inv.target.as_str(),"read"|"always"){continue;}
        for p in &bound.programs {if p.program.kind!=ProgramKind::Mutation{continue;}
            let relevant=ir::write_tables(&p.program).iter().any(|(table,kind)|table==&inv.table&&(inv.target=="write"||inv.target==*kind||*kind=="upsert"));
            if relevant{let mut op=inv.clone();op.operation=Some(p.program.name.clone());assertions.push(op);}
        }
    }
    for inv in &assertions{
        if out.exhausted(){break;}
        if out.violations.iter().any(|v|v.invariant_site==inv.site.to_string()&&v.reachability.is_reachable()){continue;}
        if inv.target=="read"&&inv.column.as_deref().is_some_and(|c|c!="id"){continue;}
        if sites.is_some_and(|sites|!sites.contains(&inv.site.to_string())){continue;}
        if inv.operation.is_none()&&discharged.contains(&inv.site.to_string()){continue;}
        if let Err(why)=operation_preflight(bound,inv){out.unsupported.insert(why);continue;}
        let mut found=false;let mut seen=BTreeSet::new();
        let combinations=bound.schema.tables.values().flat_map(|t|t.columns.values()).filter_map(|k|if let C::Enum{variants}=k.required(){Some(variants.len())}else{None}).fold(1usize,usize::saturating_mul).max(24);
        if combinations>512{out.unsupported.insert("schema enum Cartesian matrix exceeds 512 samples; remaining tuples are not covered".into());}
        for sample in 0..=combinations.min(512) {
            if !out.reserve(1){break;}
            let variant=sample.saturating_sub(1);
            let mut rows=match snapshot(bound,inv,variant){Ok(r)=>r,Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(e);break;}};
            // Try explicit policy field literals before the unchanged enum
            // matrix. A value such as status='cancelled' need not wait behind
            // hundreds of unrelated enum tuples. This is only a candidate;
            // ordinary validation and engine replay still decide refutation.
            if sample==0 {
                fn pin(rule:&RuleExpr,row:&mut Value)->bool{match rule{
                    RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Field(f),RuleTerm::Literal(v))|RuleExpr::Ne(RuleTerm::Field(f),RuleTerm::Literal(v))|
                    RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Literal(v),RuleTerm::Field(f))|RuleExpr::Ne(RuleTerm::Literal(v),RuleTerm::Field(f))=>{
                        if let Value::Row(fields)=row&&fields.contains_key(f){fields.insert(f.clone(),v.clone());true}else{false}
                    },
                    RuleExpr::And(xs)|RuleExpr::Or(xs)=>xs.iter().fold(false,|any,r|pin(r,row)||any),
                    RuleExpr::Not(r)=>pin(r,row),_=>false,
                }}
                if !inv.policy.as_ref().zip(rows.get_mut(&inv.table).and_then(|rs|rs.first_mut())).is_some_and(|(p,row)|pin(p,row)){continue;}
            }
            let candidate_args=inv.operation.as_ref().and_then(|op|bound.programs.iter().find(|p|&p.program.name==op)).and_then(|p|arguments(&p.program.args,variant));
            // Pruned dependencies can repeat after unrelated schema enum digits.
            // Identical seed/typed-argument candidates are one search input.
            if !seen.insert(serde_json::to_string(&(&rows,&candidate_args)).unwrap()){continue;}
            let mut seeded=match engine(bound,&rows,program("$security.seed",ProgramKind::Query,vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Get(Read{site:"security read".into(),table:inv.table.clone(),index:"byId".into(),key:vec![Expr::Literal(id(&inv.table))],provenance:KeyProvenance::Computed}))])){Ok(e)=>e,Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(e);continue;}};
            let rows=match readback(&seeded){Ok(r)=>r,Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(e);continue;}};
            let Some(row)=rows.get(&inv.table).and_then(|r|r.first())else{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: no generated ordinary row",inv.table));break;};
            for viewer in [VIEWER,OTHER,"account:security-no-role","service:security"]{
                if !out.reserve(1){break;}
                if inv.target=="always" {
                    match policy(bound,inv,&rows,viewer,None,row){
                        Ok(false)=>{out.attempted+=1;out.admitted+=1;out.violations.push(Counterexample{reachability:Reachability::TrustedSeedOnly,history:Vec::new(),observations:None,invariant_site:inv.site.to_string(),args:BTreeMap::new(),viewer:viewer.into(),operation:"$security.seed_at".into(),effect:"always".into(),row:row.clone(),old:None,supporting_rows:rows.clone(),rule_path:"trusted seed ingress; all typed and final-exists constraints rechecked".into(),scope:"actual seed_at commit/read-back; ordinary application reachability is not claimed".into()});found=true;},
                        Ok(true)=>{out.attempted+=1;},Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(e);}
                    }if found{break;}continue;
                }
                if let Some(operation)=&inv.operation {
                    let Some(p)=bound.programs.iter().find(|p|&p.program.name==operation)else{continue;};
                    if ephemeral_operation(bound,&p.program,&mut out){continue;}
                    let permitted=match policy(bound,inv,&rows,viewer,None,row){Ok(p)=>p,Err(why)=>{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{operation}: operation intent not judged: {why}"));continue;}};
                    let Some(args)=arguments(&p.program.args,variant)else{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{operation}: arguments need fixture assets or unsupported samples"));continue;};
                    if !out.reserve(1){break;}
                    out.attempted+=1;
                    let mut seeded=match engine(bound,&rows,program("$security.seed",ProgramKind::Query,vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Literal(Value::Null))])){Ok(e)=>e,Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(e);continue;}};
                    let args=match materialize_arguments(&mut seeded,&p.program.args,&args,viewer){Ok(a)=>a,Err(why)=>{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{operation}: argument ledger unavailable: {why}"));continue;}};
                    match seeded.mutate(operation,None,Context::new(viewer,args.clone()).at(NOW)) {
                        Ok(result) if matches!(result.state,snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent{..})=>{
                            let current=readback(&seeded).unwrap_or_default();
                            let changed=current.get(&inv.table).into_iter().flatten().filter(|r|!rows.get(&inv.table).is_some_and(|old|old.contains(r))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
                            for next in changed {
                                let old=rows.get(&inv.table).into_iter().flatten().find(|old|old.field("id").ok()==next.field("id").ok());
                                // An upsert must be attributed to its executed arm;
                                // a column contract cannot be refuted by editing a sibling.
                                if inv.target=="update"&&old.is_none() || inv.target=="insert"&&old.is_some() || inv.target=="delete" {continue;}
                                if let Some(column)=&inv.column && old.is_some_and(|old|old.field(column).ok()==next.field(column).ok()){continue;}
                                if !permitted{out.admitted+=1;out.violations.push(Counterexample{reachability:Reachability::SyntheticOperation,history:Vec::new(),observations:None,invariant_site:inv.site.to_string(),args:args.clone(),viewer:viewer.into(),operation:operation.clone(),effect:if old.is_some(){"update"}else{"insert"}.into(),row:next.clone(),old:old.cloned(),supporting_rows:rows.clone(),rule_path:format!("authored operation {operation}"),scope:"actual authored mutation committed a changed image from a schema-valid seeded snapshot".into()});found=true;break;}
                            }
                        },_=>out.refused+=1,
                    }
                    if found{break;}continue;
                }
                for word in super::effects(inv){
                    let mut admission_rows=rows.clone();if word=="insert"{admission_rows.remove(&inv.table);}
                    let judged=if word=="read"{policy_in(bound,inv,&admission_rows,viewer,Some(row),row,&mut seeded)}else{policy(bound,inv,&admission_rows,viewer,(word!="insert").then_some(row),row)};
                    let allowed=match judged{Ok(v)=>v,Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(e);continue;}};
                    if allowed{continue;}
                    if !out.reserve(1){break;}
                    out.attempted+=1;
                    let replayed=if word=="read" {seeded.query("$security.seed",Context::new(viewer,BTreeMap::new()).at(NOW)).map(|q|(q.data!=Value::Null,row.clone())).map_err(|e|e.to_string())}else{replay(bound,inv,&rows,viewer,word,row)};
                    match replayed{
                        Ok((false,_))=>out.refused+=1,
                        Ok((true,next))=>{
                            let mut args=BTreeMap::new();
                            if word=="update"{let changes=bound.schema.tables[&inv.table].columns.keys().filter(|c|row.field(c).ok()!=next.field(c).ok()).filter_map(|c|next.field(c).ok().map(|v|(c.clone(),v.clone()))).collect();args.insert("$syntheticPatch".into(),Value::Map(changes));}
                            out.admitted+=1;out.violations.push(Counterexample{reachability:Reachability::SyntheticOperation,history:Vec::new(),observations:None,invariant_site:inv.site.to_string(),args,viewer:viewer.into(),operation:format!("$security.{}.{}",inv.table,word),effect:word.into(),row:next,old:(word=="update"||word=="delete").then(||row.clone()),supporting_rows:admission_rows.clone(),rule_path:bound.schema.tables[&inv.table].rules.for_effect(super::effect(word)).quarry(),scope:if word=="update"{"schema-valid seeded snapshot; old-image policy false at an actual changed update; committed next image and patch shown; application reachability is not claimed".into()}else{"schema-valid seeded snapshot; synthetic engine table operation; application reachability is not claimed".into()}});found=true;break;},
                        Err(e)=>{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{}.{}: {e}",inv.table,word));},
                    }
                }
                if found{break;}
            }
            if found{break;}
        }
    }
    column_reads::generated(bound,&mut out,sites);
    paired::run(bound,&mut out,sites);
    timed::run(bound,&mut out,sites);
    out.unsupported.insert("unauthenticated HTTP attempts require a live server; engine principals are authenticated contexts".into());
    out.unsupported.insert("offline/revoked-device access and retained history require device boundary qualification".into());out
}
pub fn apply(report:&mut Report,campaign:&Campaign){
    report.campaign_coverage.extend(campaign.unsupported.iter().cloned());
    let rank=|c:&Counterexample|match c.reachability{Reachability::AuthoredFixtureTrace=>0,Reachability::GeneratedFixtureTrace=>1,_=>2};
    let committed=|c:&Counterexample|c.history.iter().filter(|s|s.result.get("state").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)==Some("sent")).count();
    for c in &campaign.violations {for v in &mut report.invariants {if v.invariant.site.to_string()!=c.invariant_site{continue;}
        if v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|old|rank(old)<rank(c)||rank(old)==rank(c)&&committed(old)<=committed(c)){continue;}
        v.status=Status::Refuted;v.counterexample=Some(c.clone());
        v.reasons.push("concrete policy-false snapshot admitted by the actual engine; fixture origin is explicit, not an empty-state reachability theorem".into());
    }}
}

fn arguments(args:&BTreeMap<String,ir::ArgType>,variant:usize)->Option<BTreeMap<String,Value>>{
    use ir::ArgType as A;
    fn one(k:&A,v:usize)->Option<Value>{Some(match k{
        A::Ref{table}=>id(table),A::Principal=>Value::Id(if v&1==0{OTHER}else{VIEWER}.into()),A::Id=>Value::Id("security-argument".into()),A::Cursor=>Value::Null,A::Optional(inner)=>if v&4==0{Value::Null}else{one(inner,v)?},
        A::Text{min,max,..}=>Value::String("z".repeat((*min).max(1).min(*max) as usize)),A::Enum{variants}=>Value::String(variants.get(v%variants.len())?.clone()),A::Int|A::Decimal{..}|A::Money{..}=>Value::Int(1),A::IntRange{min,max}=>Value::Int(1i64.clamp(*min,*max)),A::Time=>Value::Int(NOW+86_400_000),A::Bool=>Value::Bool(v&2==0),A::List{of:Some(inner),..}=>Value::Array(vec![one(inner,v)?]),A::ListRange{of:Some(inner),min,..}=>Value::Array((0..*min).map(|_|one(inner,v)).collect::<Option<_>>()?),A::List{..}=>Value::Array(Vec::new()),A::Json{..}=>Value::Null,A::Bytes{..}=>Value::Bytes(Vec::new()),A::Image{..}=>Value::String("$security:image".into()),A::File{..}=>Value::String("$security:file".into()),_=>return None,
    })}
    args.iter().map(|(n,k)|one(k,variant).map(|v|(n.clone(),v))).collect()
}

fn materialize_arguments(engine:&mut Engine,args:&BTreeMap<String,ir::ArgType>,values:&BTreeMap<String,Value>,viewer:&str)->Result<BTreeMap<String,Value>,String>{
    fn one(e:&mut Engine,k:&ir::ArgType,v:&Value,viewer:&str)->Result<Value,String>{Ok(match (k,v){
        (ir::ArgType::Optional(inner),v) if *v!=Value::Null=>one(e,inner,v,viewer)?,
        (ir::ArgType::List{of:Some(inner),..}|ir::ArgType::ListRange{of:Some(inner),..},Value::Array(xs))=>Value::Array(xs.iter().map(|v|one(e,inner,v,viewer)).collect::<Result<_,_>>()?),
        (ir::ArgType::Image{..},Value::String(marker)) if marker=="$security:image"=>e.store_asset(viewer,&PNG,NOW).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.column_value(),
        (ir::ArgType::File{types,..},Value::String(marker)) if marker=="$security:file"=>assets::file(e,viewer,types)?,
        _=>v.clone(),
    })}
    values.iter().map(|(n,v)|one(engine,&args[n],v,viewer).map(|v|(n.clone(),v))).collect()
}

/// Fixture-free campaigns retain empty-start bootstraps and populated role worlds.
/// The two initial states share the existing 512-single/512-pair work envelope.
pub fn generated_campaign(bound:&Bound,campaign:&mut Campaign,matrix:bool){
    for (name,_) in bound.schema.visible_tables().filter(|(_,t)|t.ephemeral.is_some()){campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("ephemeral {name}: generated memory populations and ephemeral mutation histories remain uncovered; durable campaigns use isolated hub copies"));}
    campaign.history_limit=64;campaign.generated_fixture=false;
    if !campaign.reserve(1){return;}
    match engine_with(bound,&BTreeMap::new(),Vec::new()){
        Ok(empty)=>fixture_observers(bound,&empty,campaign),
        Err(why)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("empty initial campaign unavailable: {why}"));}
    }
    campaign.history_limit=448;campaign.generated_fixture=true;
    match generated_fixture(bound,campaign){
        Ok(fixture)=>if matrix{operations(bound,&fixture,campaign)}else{fixture_observers(bound,&fixture,campaign)},
        Err(why)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("generated fixture campaign unavailable: {why}"));}
    }
    campaign.history_limit=0;campaign.generated_fixture=false;
}
/// Exercise every authored query/mutation with cross-principal candidates.
/// This is conformance exploration, not a guessed spec oracle: only declared
/// policies and replayed violations can fail security acceptance.
pub fn fixture_observers(bound:&Bound,fixture:&Engine,campaign:&mut Campaign){
    let first=campaign.violations.len();
    column_reads::direct_fixture(bound,fixture,campaign);
    histories::initial_observers(bound,fixture,campaign);
    histories::lifecycle_observers(bound,fixture,campaign);
    column_reads::fixture(bound,fixture,campaign);
    if !campaign.generated_fixture {trusted_reads(bound,fixture,campaign);}
    histories::run(bound,fixture,campaign);
    if campaign.generated_fixture {for witness in &mut campaign.violations[first..] {
        if witness.reachability==Reachability::AuthoredFixtureTrace {witness.reachability=Reachability::GeneratedFixtureTrace;witness.scope="actual authored observation from a validated generated initial fixture; fixture initialization is not claimed application-reachable".into();}
    }}
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#143-concrete-role-refutations-and-coupled-worlds — failed implication only orders a concrete, authored replay.
pub(super) fn direct_refutations(bound:&Bound,campaign:&mut Campaign){
    let first=campaign.violations.len();
    campaign.generated_fixture=true;
    match generated_fixture(bound,campaign){
        Ok(fixture)=>{
            column_reads::direct_fixture(bound,&fixture,campaign);
            histories::initial_observers(bound,&fixture,campaign);
        },
        Err(why)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("direct read witness unavailable: {why}"));}
    }
    for v in &mut campaign.violations[first..]{
        if v.reachability==Reachability::AuthoredFixtureTrace{
            v.reachability=Reachability::GeneratedFixtureTrace;
            v.scope="actual authored observation from an insert-admitted generated fixture; initialization is not claimed reachable from an empty application".into();
        }
    }
    campaign.generated_fixture=false;
}
pub fn operations(bound:&Bound,fixture:&Engine,campaign:&mut Campaign){
    let first=campaign.violations.len();
    fixture_observers(bound,fixture,campaign);
    assets::run(bound,fixture,campaign);
    let fixtures=match readback(fixture){Ok(r)=>r,Err(e)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(e);return;}};
    let has_fixture=fixtures.values().any(|r|!r.is_empty());
    if fixtures.values().map(Vec::len).sum::<usize>()>1000{campaign.unsupported.insert("operation fixture matrix exceeds 1000 rows; provide a focused security fixture".into());return;}
    let mut viewers=histories::viewers(bound);
    for (table,rows) in &fixtures{for row in rows{for (c,k) in &bound.schema.tables[table].columns{if matches!(k.required(),C::Principal)&&let Ok(Value::Id(p))=row.field(c)&&!viewers.contains(p){viewers.push(p.clone());}}}}
    let eligible=bound.programs.iter().filter(|p|matches!(p.program.kind,ProgramKind::Query|ProgramKind::Mutation)&&!p.program.native).count();
    let quota=(8192/eligible.max(1)).clamp(1,512);let mut remaining=8192usize;
    for p in &bound.programs{
        if !matches!(p.program.kind,ProgramKind::Query|ProgramKind::Mutation)||p.program.native{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: trusted/system/opaque operation",p.program.name));continue;}
        if ephemeral_operation(bound,&p.program,campaign){continue;}
        let target=bound.schema.visible_tables().find(|(t,_)|super::audit::mentions(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program).unwrap(),t)).or_else(||bound.schema.visible_tables().next()).map(|(t,_)|t.clone());
        let Some(target)=target else{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: no table population for generated arguments",p.program.name));continue;};
        let dummy=Invariant{table:target,target:"read".into(),column:None,predicate:"allow".into(),site:crate::Site::default(),policy:Some(RuleExpr::Allow),operation:Some(p.program.name.clone()),requirements:Vec::new(),syntax:None,unsupported:None};
        let cases=histories::fixture_cases(bound,&p.program,&fixtures,&viewers,campaign);
        let mut exercised=0;
        'cases:for (variant,mut args) in cases.into_iter().enumerate(){
            let rows=if has_fixture{fixtures.clone()}else{match snapshot(bound,&dummy,variant){Ok(r)=>r,Err(e)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: {e}",p.program.name));break;}}};
            if !has_fixture{for (arg,kind) in &p.program.args {if let ir::ArgType::Ref{table}=kind&&let Some(row)=rows.get(table).and_then(|rs|rs.first())&&let Ok(id)=row.field("id"){args.insert(arg.clone(),id.clone());}}}
            for viewer in &viewers{
                if exercised==quota||remaining==0{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: operation matrix capped at {quota} calls to share the 8192-call budget across every operation; remaining arguments/viewers not covered",p.program.name));break 'cases;}
                exercised+=1;remaining-=1;
                let mut engine=match if has_fixture {fork(bound,fixture,Vec::new())}else{engine(bound,&rows,program("$security.matrix",ProgramKind::Query,vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Literal(Value::Null))]))}{Ok(e)=>e,Err(e)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: {e}",p.program.name));continue;}};
                let args=match materialize_arguments(&mut engine,&p.program.args,&args,viewer){Ok(a)=>a,Err(why)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: argument ledger unavailable: {why}",p.program.name));continue;}};
                campaign.attempted+=1;*campaign.operations.entry(p.program.name.clone()).or_default()+=1;
                if p.program.kind==ProgramKind::Query{
                    match engine.query(&p.program.name,Context::new(viewer,args.clone()).at(NOW)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e) if e.code=="E_INPUT"=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: generated arguments rejected as E_INPUT",p.program.name));},Err(_)=>campaign.refused+=1,}
                }else{
                    let trace=executed::trace(bound,&p.program);
                    match engine.mutate(&p.program.name,None,Context::new(viewer,args.clone()).at(NOW).with_fixture_trace(trace.clone())){
                        Ok(result) if matches!(result.state,snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent{..})=>{
                            if let Ok(after)=readback(&engine){
                                let steps=vec![histories::Step{operation:p.program.name.clone(),viewer:viewer.clone(),args:args.clone(),result:serde_json::to_value(&result.state).unwrap()}];
                                let first_observation=campaign.violations.len();
                                executed::record(bound,&p.program,&trace,&result.state,&after,&rows,viewer,&steps,&mut engine,campaign);
                                if !has_fixture{for v in &mut campaign.violations[first_observation..]{v.reachability=Reachability::SyntheticOperation;v.scope="authored matrix operation on an invented schema snapshot; no trusted fixture or initialization trace".into();}}
                            }
                        },
                        Ok(_)=>campaign.refused+=1,
                        Err(e)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: matrix engine error {e}",p.program.name));},
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if campaign.generated_fixture{for witness in &mut campaign.violations[first..]{if witness.reachability==Reachability::AuthoredFixtureTrace{witness.reachability=Reachability::GeneratedFixtureTrace;witness.scope="actual authored matrix observation from validated generated fixture; initialization not claimed application-reachable".into();}}}
}

fn ephemeral_operation(bound:&Bound,p:&Program,out:&mut Campaign)->bool{
    let unsupported=p.kind==ProgramKind::Mutation&&bound.schema.operations.get(&p.name).is_some_and(|f|f.ephemeral);
    if unsupported{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: ephemeral mutation history is not covered by the durable campaign",p.name));}
    unsupported
}

fn fork(_bound:&Bound,fixture:&Engine,probes:Vec<Program>)->Result<Engine,String>{
    if !probes.is_empty(){return Err("fixture probes must be authored operations".into());}
    fixture.fork_fixture().map_err(|e|e.to_string())
}

// Authored seed/fixture data is an explicit trusted initial assumption. A raw
// row-read admission witness is failing; column privacy still needs an actual
// authored observer and synthetic mutations remain supplemental.
fn trusted_reads(bound:&Bound,fixture:&Engine,out:&mut Campaign){
    let Ok(rows)=readback(fixture)else{return;};
    let Ok(mut judge)=fixture.fork_fixture()else{return;};
    let actors=histories::actors(bound,&rows);
    for inv in bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|i.target=="read"&&i.column.is_none()){
        if inv.policy.as_ref().is_some_and(|policy|kernel::implies(&bound.schema.tables[&inv.table].rules.read,policy)==Ok(true)){continue;}
        if rows.get(&inv.table).is_some_and(|rs|rs.len()>1000){out.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: raw authored fixture admission samples the first 1000 rows; remaining rows uncovered",inv.target_label()));}
        'rows:for row in rows.get(&inv.table).into_iter().flatten().take(1000){for viewer in &actors{
            if !out.reserve(1){return;}
            if !live(&bound.schema.tables[&inv.table],row)||!matches!(judge.fixture_policy(&bound.schema.tables[&inv.table].rules.read,viewer,None,row,NOW),Ok(rules::Verdict::Readable))||policy_in(bound,inv,&rows,viewer,None,row,&mut judge)!=Ok(false){continue;}
            out.violations.push(Counterexample{reachability:Reachability::AuthoredFixtureTrace,invariant_site:inv.site.to_string(),args:BTreeMap::new(),viewer:viewer.clone(),operation:"$fixture.read-admission".into(),effect:"read".into(),row:row.clone(),old:None,supporting_rows:rows.clone(),rule_path:"ordinary row-read gate admits authored fixture data contrary to declared intent".into(),scope:"authored fixture initialization is trusted; raw row admission, no initialization history claimed".into(),observations:None,history:Vec::new()});
            break 'rows;
        }}
    }
}

pub(super) fn review(project:&Project,sources:&[(String,String)],notes:&[snapback4_lang::Diagnostic],ack:Option<(&str,&str)>)->Result<Vec<Disposition>,String>{
    if project.sources().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?!=sources{return Err("Quarry sources changed during security review; rerun check".into());}
    let mut sorted=sources.to_vec();sorted.sort_by(|a,b|a.0.cmp(&b.0));
    let fingerprint=hash(&serde_json::to_vec(&sorted).unwrap());
    let path=project.schema_dir().join("security-reviews.json");
    // Keep the lock inode in ignored generated output. Do not unlink a lock
    // while another process can be waiting on that inode. Kernel ownership
    // releases it on exit, including an interrupted writer.
    let _writer_lock=if ack.is_some(){
        let directory=project.schema_dir().join("generated");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&directory).map_err(|e|format!("cannot create security review lock directory: {e}"))?;
        let lock=std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true).open(directory.join("security-reviews.lock")).map_err(|e|format!("cannot open security review lock: {e}"))?;
        lock.lock().map_err(|e|format!("cannot acquire security review lock: {e}"))?;Some(lock)
    }else{None};
    if project.sources().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?!=sources{return Err("Quarry sources changed while waiting for security review; rerun check".into());}
    let mut file:File=match std::fs::read(&path){
        Ok(bytes)=>serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_|"invalid snapback/security-reviews.json; expected version 1 with per-note source/analyzer/reason records".to_string())?,
        Err(e) if e.kind()==std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound=>File{version:1,entries:BTreeMap::new()},
        Err(e)=>return Err(format!("cannot read security dispositions: {e}")),
    };
    if file.version!=1||file.entries.iter().any(|(key,e)|!digest(key)||!digest(&e.sources)||e.reason.trim().is_empty()||e.analyzer.is_empty()){return Err("invalid security disposition version/digest/reason".into());}
    if let Some((key,reason))=ack{
        if reason.trim().is_empty(){return Err("--reason needs the specification rationale for this individual note".into());}
        if !notes.iter().any(|n|id(n)==key){return Err("--ack-security ID is not a current security note; run check --json".into());}
        file.entries.insert(key.into(),Entry{sources:fingerprint.clone(),analyzer:ANALYZER.into(),reason:reason.trim().into()});
        let temporary=path.with_extension(format!("json.{}.tmp",std::process::id()));
        let result=std::fs::write(&temporary,serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&file).unwrap()).and_then(|_|{
            if project.sources()?!=sources{return Err(std::io::Error::other("Quarry sources changed before disposition publication; rerun check"));}
            std::fs::rename(&temporary,&path)
        });
        if let Err(e)=result{let _=std::fs::remove_file(&temporary);return Err(format!("cannot record security disposition: {e}"));}
    }
    Ok(notes.iter().map(|n|{let key=id(n);let entry=file.entries.get(&key).filter(|e|e.sources==fingerprint&&e.analyzer==ANALYZER);
        Disposition{id:key,code:n.code.clone(),site:n.site.to_string(),gated:gated(&n.code),acknowledged:entry.is_some(),reason:entry.map(|e|e.reason.clone())}
    }).collect())
}
pub(super) fn pending(dispositions:&[Disposition])->bool{dispositions.iter().any(|d|d.gated&&!d.acknowledged)}
pub(super) fn print(dispositions:&[Disposition]){for d in dispositions.iter().filter(|d|d.gated||d.acknowledged){
    if d.acknowledged{println!("security reviewed {} {}: {}",d.id,d.code,d.reason.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));}
    else{println!("security review required {} {} at {}; repair or check --ack-security {} --reason '<spec rationale>'",d.id,d.code,d.site,d.id);}
}}

//! Repairs lead; uncertainty stays visible without repeating every proof blocker.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#144-actions-precede-coverage-details — advice is separate from replayed failures.
use super::{Report, Status};

/// One consequence ordering shared by check and audit. Lower means more urgent.
pub fn note_priority(code: &str) -> u8 {
    match code {
        "N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT" | "N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE" => 0,
        "N_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION" | "N_SELF_CLAIMED_RELATIONSHIP" => 1,
        "N_GRANT_OUTLIVES_ROLE" | "N_OPTIONAL_EVIDENCE" | "N_ROLE_WIDE_READ" |
        "N_BROAD_READ" | "N_CALLER_TIME" | "N_SWEEP_ONLY_DEADLINE" |
        "N_CREATION_REASON" | "N_CREATION_MONEY" | "N_CONSTANT_APPROVAL" |
        "N_TRANSITION_BYPASS" | "N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK" | "N_DURATION_BOUNDS" |
        "N_ROLE_WIDE_WRITE" => 2,
        "N_COLUMN_RESULT_EXPOSURE" | "N_INSERT_WRITE_INTENT" => 5,
        "N_INVARIANT_RESTATES_RULE" => 6,
        "N_SECURITY_INTENT" => 7,
        _ => 4,
    }
}

impl Report {
    /// Full structured evidence remains in the report; this is a human action list.
    pub fn action_text(&self, limit: usize) -> String {
        let failures = self.invariants.iter().filter(|v| v.status == Status::Refuted &&
            v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.reachability.is_reachable())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let mut notes = self.notes.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        notes.sort_by_key(|n| (note_priority(&n.code), n.site.file.clone(), n.site.line, n.site.col, &n.code, &n.message));
        notes.dedup_by(|a,b| a.site == b.site && a.code == b.code && a.message == b.message);
        let mut out = format!("security actions: {} fix{}, {} review{}\n", failures.len(),
            if failures.len() == 1 { "" } else { "es" }, notes.len(), if notes.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" });
        for v in &failures {
            let c = v.counterexample.as_ref().unwrap();
            out.push_str(&format!("  FIX {}: {} via {} as {} ({}); tighten enforcement to the declared intent, then run snapback4 test\n",
                v.invariant.site, v.invariant.target_label(), c.operation, c.viewer, serde_json::to_value(&c.reachability).unwrap().as_str().unwrap()));
        }
        let mut shown = 0;
        for note in notes.iter().enumerate().filter_map(|(i,n)|
            (i < limit || note_priority(&n.code) <= 2).then_some(*n)) {
            shown += 1;
            out.push_str(&format!("  REVIEW {} {}: {}\n    {}\n",note.site,note.code,note.message,note.rewrite));
        }
        if shown < notes.len() { out.push_str(&format!("  {} more reviews: snapback4 audit --all or check --verbose\n", notes.len()-shown)); }
        let proved = self.invariants.iter().filter(|v| v.status == Status::Proved).count();
        let refuted = self.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==Status::Refuted).count();
        let unproved = self.invariants.len()-proved-refuted;
        out.push_str(&format!("security: {proved} proved, {refuted} refuted, {unproved} unproved ({} failing)\n", failures.len()));
        let supplemental = self.invariants.iter().filter(|v| v.status == Status::Refuted &&
            v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| !c.reachability.is_reachable())).count();
        if supplemental > 0 {out.push_str(&format!("  {supplemental} seed/synthetic observations are non-failing\n"));}
        if unproved > 0 || !self.campaign_coverage.is_empty() {
            out.push_str(&format!("  next: snapback4 test; {} coverage gaps (audit --all/JSON keeps every reason)\n",self.campaign_coverage.len()));
        }
        if self.invariants.is_empty() {out.push_str("  next: answer snapback/generated/security-invariants.q.draft from the spec; declare intent and run snapback4 test\n");}
        out
    }
}

# Security invariants

State privacy intent separately from enforcement. Check reports proved, refuted
with a replayed counterexample, or unproved with a reason; passing finite tests
are not proofs.

```quarry
table privateNotes:
  patient: principal
  body: text 1..2000
  sealed: bool default false
  read <- .patient = viewer and .sealed = false
  insert <- .patient = viewer and .sealed = false
  online only
-- Spec: a patient may see only their own note; sealing may narrow availability.
-- Removing an accidental broad branch from the rule must not change this intent.
invariant privateNotes.read only .patient = viewer
invariant privateNotes.body read only .patient = viewer
invariant privateNotes.insert only .patient = viewer
query privateNote(note: privateNotes):
  return privateNotes[note]
mutation writePrivateNote(body: text 1..2000):
  return insert privateNotes { patient: viewer, body }
```

## Reference

`invariant table.column read only P` protects a column value, derived values and value-dependent counts/existence/refusals. Mutation results, implicit final writes and explicit returned row objects are observers too. A query projection alone is not privacy: use column read rules to protect every operation. An authored projection excluding the column does not by itself disclose that value; filtering, ordering or copying it can. Audit JSON includes `column_audiences` (effective row rule plus private-owner gate). Unknown derived and opaque paths remain unproved.

`invariant table.read only P` protects read intent; insert, update and delete
name authority. `invariant table.column write only P` covers writes to a
column (insert, inserted insert-if-absent, update and both upsert arms).
Creation is not exempt from write intent; tests judge each executed write in
a committed mutation, including intermediate writes in a multi-write operation. `invariant table.column update only P` checks
only edits, retaining old-and-next-image semantics; use it when creation is permitted
to a different role (for example counter staff creating a ticket price). `invariant table always P` states row integrity.
An update policy over `.field` constrains **both old and next images**.
A policy saying status must not be override therefore also restricts editing
a row that was already override, even when changing it away from that status.
For the role authority of one named mutation, use operation-specific intent
(`invariant table.operation only P`) instead. General next-image-only and
cross-operation transition assertions still need a separate reduction.
Predicates use the existing rule vocabulary: `.field`, `viewer`, `exists`,
comparisons, `and`, `or`, `not`. For a role write use the complete roster probe,
for example `invariant members.role write only exists roles[viewer, role = 'owner']`
in a schema declaring those tables. A declaration never grants authority. Whole-row read intent also protects logical
existence: when occupancy totals are intentionally public but roster identities
are private, declare column read intent for those identities instead. Include
a service seat explicitly when the spec permits it; seats are ordinary checked
viewers, never implicitly exempt.

The implemented proof fragment exhaustively checks independent three-valued
rule predicates. A failed implication is unproved until an engine replay
establishes a counterexample. A schema-valid seeded snapshot is not a claim
that an application operation sequence reaches that state. Required-column
non-null assertions have a separate validation theorem. Read/count/sum/existence obligations are reported separately. A maintained aggregate with bare privacy keys can prove its contributor audience; a broader aggregate can yield a paired present/absent counterexample. Exact server `not before`/`expire at` bounds can prove a temporal read component independently of physical sweeps. General transitions and unsupported expressions remain unproved.
Read-through captures/live parents, complex derived aggregates, raw rule probes,
owned-field update bypasses, cascade/set-null and opaque jobs/workers need
separate reductions. An unresolved path blocks the whole declaration's proof.

Server delivery authorizes against the current server snapshot. A disconnected
device can retain an earlier snapshot until it receives a revocation; even
`until-revoked` cannot know a later server role. Synced current-role intent is
therefore unproved for device access. Retained history follows its leave policy.
These reports exclude physical timing and resource/meter side channels and
explicitly exclude the trusted system-principal boundary. Service seats remain
inside the ordinary-viewer check; there is no implicit seat exemption.

## Current roles and derived grants

A membership or assignment created while a user is an inspector can survive
their demotion. Conjoin the **current reader's role** with the assignment
branch, or revoke every derived grant transactionally whenever the role changes.
A grant writer's role does not establish the recipient's current authority.
With independent current-role intent, grant-lifetime advice points at this pattern; the argument-grant advice identifies
arguments written into reader-grant columns: validate the chosen principal's
role and relationship, even when the caller is privileged.
Global admin authority must come from a trusted operator or existing admin;
a group-creation `created` probe must remain scoped to that group everywhere.
`N_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION` identifies role assignments trusted by later rules without independent delegation. Open enrollment may be intentional: compare each note with the specification. See `guide staging` for operator first-admin setup and `guide sharing` for parent authority.

## Required evidence and deadlines

If the spec requires a photo, use a required `image <=5000000` column or
`[image <=5000000] 1..4`; `?` permits omission and `[image] <=4` permits zero.
Uploads are verified media and asset reads inherit row and private-field rules.
Optional-evidence advice asks the builder to check intentional optionality.
Text `min..max` counts non-whitespace Unicode characters toward the minimum;
the maximum counts all characters. Stored text is not trimmed or rewritten.
A sweep changes state eventually: compare the deadline with server `now` in
the mutation too if writes must stop exactly at that instant.

## Existence observations

A lookup that says NOT_FOUND on absence followed by a denial saying FORBIDDEN
can reveal existence to callers admitted by a broader read rule. Use the same
code **and message** for hidden/absent/denied cases when existence is private,
or tighten the table read rule. Program `exists` is caller-filtered; probes
inside table rules inspect raw rows and can disclose predicates indirectly.
Inspect both paths in `audit`; a payload-only read check is insufficient.

## When an observer remains unproved

The report names the edge that lacks a reduction. Preserve the specification
while changing its enforcement; weakening an invariant to match a leaking
rule does not repair privacy.

separate finite successor bound. Check keeps its shared 512-work/1500ms limit.
Frontier, argument, signature and attempt cuts remain coverage gaps. Synthetic
observations are REVIEW, while actual admitted histories from validated generated
fixtures retain their generated-fixture-trace origin and can fail acceptance.

### N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT

N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT: A recipient role required when storing a grant is mutable and missing from a reader branch that trusts that grant, including column payload readers. Recheck current role or revoke derived grants. Intentional retained authority needs an individual source-bound disposition.

### N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE

N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE: An optional upload argument can be omitted while a mutation creates a parent or evidence row. Require the upload before creating the parent when the spec requires evidence. Intentional optional attachments need an individual source-bound disposition.

### N_CREATION_REASON

N_CREATION_REASON: Creating a row accepts a reason argument without a positive non-whitespace minimum. Compare the justification requirement with the spec; use text 1..N when required. This name-based question is advisory.

### N_CREATION_MONEY

N_CREATION_MONEY: Creating a row accepts omitted money. Model and require the amount when the spec requires a fee or payment; confirm intentional optional amounts against the spec. This name-based question is advisory.

### N_CONSTANT_APPROVAL

N_CONSTANT_APPROVAL: Creation stores a constant true approval/payment flag. A true constant does not verify payment or approval; record the required amount/evidence and the independently authorized decision. This name-based question is advisory.

### N_TRANSITION_BYPASS

N_TRANSITION_BYPASS: A generic enum setter reaches a state also reached by a stricter decision mutation. Apply the decision authority to every path reaching that state; write independent transition intent and run test.

### N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK

N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK: A creator checks mutable eligibility that a later approval/transition does not recheck. Decide whether eligibility must remain current and write independent intent; test create, eligibility change, approval.

### N_DURATION_BOUNDS

N_DURATION_BOUNDS: Operations apply different server-relative duration bounds to one column. Compare the windows with the specification and make them consistent or document deliberate differences.

### N_ROLE_WIDE_WRITE

N_ROLE_WIDE_WRITE: A global role plus viewer attribution does not identify the owner of this resource. Ask whether any role member may write any row; model the target-to-owner relationship and guard it. See the Wall ownership rule recipe.

# LLP 3000.036.004: Security invariants and exposure

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Accepted (SEC design revisions 3/5 and SEC2 amendment/implementation round 5: Muse and fresh Codex READY; qualification in progress)
**Systems:** Snapback 4 Quarry authorization, check, audit, generated security tests, validation
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever (SEC)
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Revised:** 2026-10-22 (SEC7 §16 design: Muse and fresh Codex READY; implementation qualification in progress); previously 2026-10-21 (SEC5 §14 and SEC6 §15; both independently reviewed; SEC6 scoped qualification complete; code snapshot4578e98bed)
**Related:** [LLP 3000.036](./3000.036-what-the-app-farm-asks-of-the-rule-language.rfc.md), [LLP 3000.035](./3000.035-quarry-semantics-in-lean.plan.md), [LLP 3000.014](./3000.014-a-child-reads-through-its-parent.rfc.md), [LLP 3000.038](./3000.038-file-assets.rfc.md)

## 1. Contract

The wave-16 bakeoff found rules enforced correctly but policies encoded wrongly.
A declaration of intent is independent of the rules implementing it. `check`
reports each declaration as **proved**, **refuted**, or **unproved**. Refuted
means a concrete, replayed database/rule counterexample, never merely a Boolean
assignment. Unproved names the unsupported path or incomplete search. Neither
unproved nor a finite passing test campaign may be described as proved.

Implementer: SEC in this worktree, starting 2026-10-18. The author commissioned
this semantic extension and two independent design reviews. No version bump
or publication is part of this lane. STAGE owns provisioning/password dev doors;
RULES5 owns live-parent rule semantics; FRONT owns general diagnostic triage.

## 2. Surface

Use the existing rule vocabulary rather than invent a second policy language:

```
invariant notes.read only .patient = viewer or .clinician = viewer
invariant requests.update only .requester != viewer
invariant members.role write only exists roles[viewer, role = 'owner']
invariant photos always .image != null
```

The first target is a table, the second component an effect (`read`, `insert`,
`update`, `delete`) or a column followed by `write`. `write` checks insert and
update, including both images for ordinary updates; delete authority has its
own declaration. A column invariant only concerns writes to that column, but
must include every effective admission path. Owner-only field patches bypass
an ordinary table update rule; invariants affected by `written by` stay
unproved until that bypass is modeled. An implication from a denied table
rule must never prove such an owned-field claim.
`always` is a row-integrity assertion. Predicates parse as ordinary Quarry
expressions; unsupported policy expressions are reported unproved with the
reason. Unknown tables/columns/effects are authoring errors. Multiple source
files and multiple declarations are supported. For update intent `.field` means both old and next images for mutable
columns; named transitions require an explicit reviewed reduction or stay
unproved. Once-judged immutable/id rules need a proved equal-image reduction
or stay unproved. Both upsert arms and `insert if absent` are included, with
their own collision/refusal observations. `always` quantifies over every
committed row image from insert/update/upsert and trusted seed/import/restore/
activation, not merely mutation inserts. Constraint-based row proof must use
the actual validation on every ingress, including defaults and the exact
non-whitespace minimum function, or stay unproved.

No declaration changes runtime
authority or replaces a rule. No implicit service-seat exemption is added.

The proof fragment uses bound rule predicates. A row assertion can be proved
from its required column type/constraints (not an optional type), or otherwise
remains unproved. Aggregate/transition/temporal assertions outside that fragment
remain explicitly unproved, not syntactically discarded. Syntax with `now`,
counts, or other program expressions must retain that reason. This is a safe
extension point, not a claim of a complete solver for arbitrary Quarry.

## 3. Sound proof boundary

For a table effect, prove `admission => policy` for **every database snapshot**,
row image, ordinary authenticated viewer (including service seats) and clock.
The engine system principal is explicitly outside this quantification: it is
the trusted seed/import/job boundary, never an ordinary user or an implicit
service-seat exemption. Tables touched by system/native/job/worker paths remain
unproved absent a reviewed reduction, and audit lists those writers. This overapproximates every reachable history:
an old assignment and a changed current role are independent facts. Grant
creation never proves a current role. Required role predicates must be true at
the access boundary. No fixture-specific assumption enters a proof.

Translate Boolean connectives compositionally, retaining true/false/unknown
truth for atomic predicates. Unknown never admits and `not unknown` is unknown.
Atomic facts are keyed by their full bound structure, including table, index,
keys, named equalities and old/next image. Symmetric equality may canonicalize by operand reordering only, preserving
Value variants (Id is not Text), table, index, keys, image and predicate kind;
other equalities and probes stay independent. A finite exhaustive implication
check over this abstraction is sound because it includes every concrete
valuation, even impossible ones. Cap atoms/work; cap exhaustion is unproved.
Do not add database consistency axioms without a separate soundness argument.
Never drop, assume true/false, or simplify an unsupported admission atom;
keep it opaque with its full identity or report unproved. Concrete leaf
semantics are the current `evaluate_leaf`/`term`, not stale Lean open points:
null equals null, null differs from a non-null literal, Id differs from Text,
noninteger ordered comparison returns false, and a missing live reference
marks unknown (including under negation). Missing ordinary fields currently
load null; missing reference and missing image are not conflated. Any semantic
mismatch with the independent model is named, never normalized away. Runtime
errors do not establish an admitted result; probe/storage/schema failure
cannot be used as a successful counterexample or a proof fact.

The Lean addition proves a three-valued Kleene kernel with admission only
on Readable and the exact theorem: exhaustive checking implies that for every
valuation, eval(admission) = Readable implies eval(policy) = Readable; the Quarry-to-kernel translation and runtime boundary remain reviewed
Rust obligations, not a claim of whole-platform formal verification.

For read intent, admission includes the ordinary read rule and every bypass:
- point/list/view/filter/count/exists and live refetch use ruled reads;
- sync acquisition and publication authorize at their own server snapshot. An
  offline device cannot know a later server revocation, even with until-revoked.
  A synced read invariant therefore reports the device access path unproved
  for current-server-role intent, separately from its server proof. Delivered
  history has an additional explicit retained-history blocker. No stale local
  role is treated as a current server role;
- inherited read-through rules are checked in their bound form, including
  captures; live-parent semantics remain RULES5's responsibility;
- valued write targets already reread through `get` before returning, and
  generated insert results also use an ordinary ruled read. Verify those
  reductions against the bound IR; any escaping image without that reduction
  is a blocker or must satisfy the implication `effective write admission => read intent` for that image;
  otherwise the declaration stays unproved;
- maintained aggregates/columns and row views may expose source changes under
  different rules: report such source claims unproved unless a reviewed exact
  reduction proves them; projections narrow payload only; existence/count disclosure follows the
  derived path's own rules, so each derived path needs its own reduction or
  stays unproved;
- table-rule probes see raw target rows, unlike program `exists`. Follow
  reverse dependencies into every other table's read/write rules: the presence
  of a marker row or a successful write can disclose the protected target's
  existence or named fields without returning that target. Source privacy
  intent remains unproved for such raw-probe observations unless a reviewed
  reduction proves authorization or the policy explicitly permits disclosure;
- incoming `on delete cascade` and `on delete set null` effects bypass child
  delete/update rules. Report child delete/update/column-write invariants
  unproved when affected, including transitive cascades, until initiating
  authority and child-image policy are modeled. Enumerate these edges in audit;
- asset reads inherit their owning row privacy, while upload/write authority
  belongs to insert/update intent; applicable private-field authorities must be conjoined with owning-row
  admission for asset reads;
- jobs, schedules, native jobs, actions and external effects are trusted system
  or worker boundaries. Read claims affected by opaque outputs/side effects
  remain unproved. Job writes do not prove ordinary-user write authority;
- refusal codes are observations: an authored difference between an absent
  lookup and later denial is a reported exposure. A privacy proof must not
  ignore that path. Unmodeled constraint/refusal observations remain unproved.

Observer boundary: this verifies row payload and logical existence/refusal
observations, not physical timing, runtime cost or all resource side channels.
The platform's documented examined-count/meter-cut observations are explicitly
excluded and reported as exclusions, not full noninterference. Read intent
includes all logical exposures above. A component may be proved while the
whole declaration remains unproved because another path is blocked.

The implementation must build a closed-world census of bound IR read/write
forms and schema-triggered paths. An unclassified form is a blocker, never
silently omitted. Census includes sequence allocation/read admission, online
and device query paths, ephemeral paths, owner fields, maintained writes and
referential actions. System/job/action/native/external touched tables default
unproved without a reviewed reduction, and are listed as grant-column writers.
Every `read` declaration covers all enumerated logical paths, not just its
direct rule. Authenticated viewer classes use engine operations; signed-out
cases run only against HTTP/auth admission, never a fabricated principal.
Retained-history observations are classified by leave policy and reported
separately; they cannot refute the platform's retention contract or prove a
current-role declaration. Test output names unsupported device freshness.

The report enumerates the paths checked and blockers. A proof is never awarded
just because the direct table rule passed while an indirect path is unmodeled.
Conservative rejection/notes are acceptable; false proof is not.

## 4. Counterexamples and generated tests

Generate deterministic challenges from schema types, policy atoms and fixture
rows. Use in-memory stores; never leave SQLite sidecars under target. Vary the
viewer across owner/other-user/other-role/revoked-role/unauthenticated classes,
policy literals, principal arguments and absent optional values. Existing role
rows and retained grant rows form revoked-role snapshots. Do not call an
arbitrary consistent snapshot a *reachable* application-operation sequence.

Concrete counterexamples must replay the engine's actual rule admission and
show the policy false, recording viewer, effect, row, supporting rows and rule
path. The absence of a concrete witness when implication fails is **unproved**.
Generated tests are a separate executable check, run by default `test`, with
coverage counts and named unsupported cases. They use isolated state so they
cannot corrupt the fixture business tests. For operations, derive arguments
from fixtures and schema, substitute other principals and roles, and compare
admitted effects/observations against the declared intent. Merely succeeding
as another user is not a failure when policy permits that operation. Signed-out

//! Real operation histories from a complete trusted fixture, including assets.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#122-reproducible-campaigns-and-reachability — only actual fixture traces establish application reachability.
use super::*;
const LIMIT:usize=512;
#[derive(Clone,Debug,Serialize,serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Step {pub operation:String,pub viewer:String,pub args:BTreeMap<String,Value>,pub result:serde_json::Value}

pub(super) fn viewers(bound:&Bound)->Vec<String>{
    let mut out=BTreeSet::from([VIEWER.into(),OTHER.into(),"account:security-no-role".into(),"service:security".into()]);
    out.extend(bound.personas.iter().map(|p|if p.contains(':'){p.clone()}else{format!("dev:{p}")}));
    fn seats(value:&serde_json::Value,out:&mut BTreeSet<String>){match value{
        serde_json::Value::String(s) if s.starts_with("service:")&&s.len()>8=>{out.insert(s.clone());},
        serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs{seats(x,out)},
        serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for x in xs.values(){seats(x,out)},_=>{}
    }}
    seats(&serde_json::to_value(&bound.schema).unwrap(),&mut out);
    for p in &bound.programs{seats(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program).unwrap(),&mut out);}
    seats(&serde_json::to_value(&bound.invariants).unwrap(),&mut out);
    out.into_iter().collect()
}
pub(super) fn actors(bound:&Bound,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>)->Vec<String>{
    let mut out=viewers(bound);
    for (table,rs) in rows{for row in rs{for (c,k) in &bound.schema.tables[table].columns{
        if matches!(k.required(),C::Principal)&&let Ok(Value::Id(p))=row.field(c)&&!out.contains(p){out.push(p.clone());}
    }}}
    out
}
pub(super) fn fixture_cases(bound:&Bound,p:&Program,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,actors:&[String],out:&mut Campaign)->Vec<BTreeMap<String,Value>>{
    let args=&p.args;
    let mut literals=BTreeMap::<String,Vec<Value>>::new();
    fn collect(value:&serde_json::Value,out:&mut BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>){
        if let Some(binary)=value.get("Binary") {for (a,b) in [("left","right"),("right","left")] {
            if let (Some(name),Some(literal))=(binary.get(a).and_then(|v|v.get("Variable")).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),binary.get(b).and_then(|v|v.get("Literal"))) {
                if let Ok(value)=serde_json::from_value::<Value>(literal.clone()){out.entry(name.into()).or_default().push(value);}
            }
        }}
        match value{serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for v in xs.values(){collect(v,out)},serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for v in xs{collect(v,out)},_=>{}}
    }
    collect(&serde_json::to_value(p).unwrap(),&mut literals);
    fn values(name:&str,k:&ir::ArgType,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,actors:&[String])->Option<Vec<Value>>{
        Some(match k{
            ir::ArgType::Enum{variants}=>variants.iter().map(|s|Value::String(s.clone())).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Text{min,max,..}=>['z','y'].into_iter().map(|c|Value::String(c.to_string().repeat((*min).max(1).min(*max) as usize))).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Int=>vec![Value::Int(0),Value::Int(1),Value::Int(2)],
            ir::ArgType::IntRange{min,max}=>{let mut xs=vec![*min,1i64.clamp(*min,*max),*max];xs.sort();xs.dedup();xs.into_iter().map(Value::Int).collect()},
            ir::ArgType::Bool=>vec![Value::Bool(false),Value::Bool(true)],
            ir::ArgType::Time=>vec![Value::Int(NOW-86_400_000),Value::Int(NOW),Value::Int(NOW+86_400_000)],
            ir::ArgType::Principal=>actors.iter().map(|s|Value::Id(s.clone())).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Ref{table} if rows.get(table).is_some_and(|rs|!rs.is_empty())=>rows[table].iter().filter_map(|r|r.field("id").ok().cloned()).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Optional(inner)=>{let mut v=vec![Value::Null];v.extend(values(name,inner,rows,actors)?);v},
            _=>vec![arguments(&BTreeMap::from([(name.into(),k.clone())]),0)?.remove(name)?],
        })
    }
    let mut cases=vec![BTreeMap::new()];
    for (name,k) in args{
        let Some(mut vals)=values(name,k,rows,actors)else{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{name}: history needs a typed asset argument"));return Vec::new();};
        for literal in literals.get(name).into_iter().flatten() {
            let valid=match (k,literal){
                (ir::ArgType::Text{min,max,..},Value::String(s))=>s.chars().filter(|c|!c.is_whitespace()).count()>=*min as usize&&s.chars().count()<=*max as usize,
                (ir::ArgType::Int,Value::Int(_))=>true,
                (ir::ArgType::IntRange{min,max},Value::Int(n))=>(*min..=*max).contains(n),_=>false,
            };
            if valid&&!vals.contains(literal){vals.insert(0,literal.clone());}
        }
        let mut next=Vec::new();
        'product:for offset in 0..vals.len(){for n in 0..cases.len().max(vals.len()){
            if out.exhausted(){return next;}
            let mut case=cases[n%cases.len()].clone();case.insert(name.clone(),vals[(n+offset)%vals.len()].clone());
            if !next.contains(&case){next.push(case);}if next.len()==LIMIT{out.unsupported.insert("history arguments capped at 512 combinations".into());break 'product;}
        }}
        cases=next;
    }
    let focused=super::executed::write_arguments(bound,p).into_iter().filter(|a|matches!(p.args.get(a),Some(ir::ArgType::Optional(_)))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if focused.is_empty(){return cases;}
    let mut prioritized=Vec::new();
    for case in cases{
        if !prioritized.contains(&case){prioritized.push(case.clone());}
        for name in &focused{if let Some(value)=arguments(&BTreeMap::from([(name.clone(),p.args[name].clone())]),4).and_then(|mut a|a.remove(name))&&value!=Value::Null{
            let mut alternate=case.clone();alternate.insert(name.clone(),value);if !prioritized.contains(&alternate){prioritized.push(alternate);}
        }}
        if prioritized.len()>=LIMIT{prioritized.truncate(LIMIT);out.unsupported.insert("column-write argument frontier capped at 512; remaining combinations uncovered".into());break;}
    }prioritized
}
// Preserve status/decision alternatives on each resource tuple before the
// small directed cap; text/noise arguments must not correlate bools with ids.
fn directed_cases(p:&Program,cases:Vec<BTreeMap<String,Value>>,campaign:&mut Campaign)->Vec<BTreeMap<String,Value>>{
    let identities=p.args.iter().filter(|(_,k)|matches!(k,ir::ArgType::Ref{..}|ir::ArgType::Principal)).map(|(n,_)|n).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let original=cases.clone();
    let mut seen=BTreeSet::new();let mut groups=Vec::new();
    for base in cases{let key=serde_json::to_string(&identities.iter().map(|n|(*n,base.get(*n))).collect::<Vec<_>>()).unwrap();if !seen.insert(key){continue;}
        let mut group=vec![base.clone()];
        for (name,kind) in &p.args{let values=match kind{ir::ArgType::Bool=>vec![Value::Bool(false),Value::Bool(true)],ir::ArgType::Enum{variants}=>variants.iter().cloned().map(Value::String).collect(),_=>Vec::new()};
            for value in values{let mut candidate=base.clone();candidate.insert(name.clone(),value);if !group.contains(&candidate){group.push(candidate);}}
        }groups.push(group);
    }
    let mut out=Vec::new();for n in 0..groups.iter().map(Vec::len).max().unwrap_or(0){for group in &groups{if let Some(args)=group.get(n){out.push(args.clone());}}}
    if original.iter().any(|case|!out.contains(case)){campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: directed argument grouping omits correlated/non-status alternatives; remaining combinations uncovered",p.name));}
    out
//! Authored write boundaries and compiler-typed committed mutation payloads.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#151-every-executed-write — no net-image inference for intermediate writes.
use super::*;
use snapback4_core::engine::fixture_trace::{Trace,Intent};
pub(super) fn trace(bound:&Bound,p:&Program)->Trace {
    Trace::new(bound.invariants.iter().filter(|inv|!matches!(inv.target.as_str(),"read"|"always")&&inv.operation.as_ref().is_none_or(|op|op==&p.name)).filter_map(|inv|Some(Intent{
        site:inv.site.to_string(),table:inv.table.clone(),column:inv.column.clone(),policy:inv.policy.clone()?,
        effects:super::super::effects(inv).iter().map(|word|super::super::effect(word)).collect(),
    })).collect())
}
pub(super) fn record(bound:&Bound,p:&Program,trace:&Trace,result:&snapback4_core::WriteState,after:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,initial:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,viewer:&str,steps:&[histories::Step],engine:&mut Engine,out:&mut Campaign){
    for observation in trace.take(){
        let Some(inv)=bound.invariants.iter().find(|inv|inv.site.to_string()==observation.site)else{continue;};
        match observation.allowed{
            Some(false)=>if let Some(row)=observation.next.as_ref().or(observation.old.as_ref()){
                if histories::violation(out,inv,steps,viewer,row,observation.old.as_ref(),initial,match observation.effect{Effect::Insert=>"insert",Effect::Update=>"update",Effect::Delete=>"delete",Effect::Read=>"read"}){
                    out.violations.last_mut().unwrap().rule_path="actual executed write boundary; independent policy false in the provisional transaction; enclosing authored mutation committed".into();
                }
            },
            None=>{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{} / {}: executed policy unknown; no refutation",p.name,inv.target_label()));},_=>{},
        }
    }
    let snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent{result:data,..}=result else{return;};
    let Some(bp)=bound.programs.iter().find(|bp|bp.program.name==p.name)else{return;};
    for inv in bound.invariants.iter().filter(|inv|inv.target=="read"){
        let Some(policy)=inv.policy.as_ref()else{continue;};
        let deps=stability::dependencies(bound,policy);
        let implicit=stability::implicit(bound,p);
        if implicit.contains(&inv.table)||implicit.iter().any(|t|deps.contains(t))||ir::write_tables(p).iter().any(|(t,_)|deps.contains(t)){
            out.unsupported.insert(format!("{} / {}: mutation-result policy changes require a disclosure-boundary reduction",p.name,inv.target_label()));continue;
        }
        for row in after.get(&inv.table).into_iter().flatten(){
            let Ok(key)=row.field("id")else{continue;};
            if !histories::typed_disclosure(&bp.result,data,&inv.table,key,inv.column.as_deref(),row){continue;}
            if !histories::typed_disclosure_image(&bp.result,data,&inv.table,key,inv.column.as_deref(),row,Some(policy)){
                out.unsupported.insert(format!("{} / {}: returned policy image differs from committed image; disclosure boundary uncovered",p.name,inv.target_label()));continue;
            }
            if !out.reserve(1){return;}
            if policy_in(bound,inv,after,viewer,None,row,engine)!=Ok(false){continue;}
            if histories::violation(out,inv,steps,viewer,row,None,initial,"mutation result"){
                let v=out.violations.last_mut().unwrap();v.operation=p.name.clone();v.args=steps.last().map(|s|s.args.clone()).unwrap_or_default();v.rule_path="authored mutation returned a compiler-typed protected row/column payload; stable current policy false".into();
            }
        }
    }
}

// Follow an actually admitted state change with payload-bearing operations on
// the same referenced row. This finds lifecycle-to-mutation observations without
// spending pair slots on unrelated roster and creation combinations.
pub(super) fn pairs(bound:&Bound,candidates:&[(&Program,String,BTreeMap<String,Value>)],committed:&[usize])->Vec<(usize,usize)>{
    let protected=bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|i.target=="read").map(|i|i.table.clone()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    let mut groups:BTreeMap<(String,String),Vec<(usize,usize)>>=BTreeMap::new();let mut seen=BTreeSet::new();
    for (second,(p,actor,args)) in candidates.iter().enumerate(){
        let Some(bp)=bound.programs.iter().find(|bp|bp.program.name==p.name)else{continue;};
        for &first in committed{
            let (before,who,inputs)=&candidates[first];if before.name==p.name{continue;}
            let shared=protected.iter().any(|table|histories::typed_source(&bp.result,table)&&ir::write_tables(before).iter().any(|(t,_)|t==table)&&before.args.iter().any(|(a,k)|matches!(k,ir::ArgType::Ref{table:t} if t==table)&&p.args.iter().any(|(b,k)|matches!(k,ir::ArgType::Ref{table:t} if t==table)&&inputs.get(a)==args.get(b))));
            if shared&&seen.insert((before.name.clone(),who.clone(),p.name.clone(),actor.clone())){groups.entry((p.name.clone(),actor.clone())).or_default().push((first,second));}
        }
    }
    let mut out=Vec::new();for n in 0..groups.values().map(Vec::len).max().unwrap_or(0){for group in groups.values(){if let Some(pair)=group.get(n){out.push(*pair);if out.len()==256{return out;}}}}out
}

// Identify direct argument supplies to declared column-write intent. This only
// prioritizes proposals; actual interpreter admission still decides every case.
pub(super) fn write_arguments(bound:&Bound,p:&Program)->BTreeSet<String>{
    fn walk(v:&serde_json::Value,f:&mut impl FnMut(&serde_json::Value)){
        f(v);match v{serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for x in xs.values(){walk(x,f)},serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs{walk(x,f)},_=>{}}
    }
    let json=serde_json::to_value(p).unwrap();let mut bindings=BTreeMap::new();
    walk(&json,&mut |v|for tag in ["Const","Let"]{if let Some(b)=v.get(tag)&&let(Some(n),Some(e))=(b.get("name").and_then(|v|v.as_str()),b.get("value")){bindings.insert(n.to_string(),e.clone());}});
    fn resolve<'a>(v:&'a serde_json::Value,bindings:&'a BTreeMap<String,serde_json::Value>,depth:usize)->&'a serde_json::Value{
        if depth>32{return v;}if let Some(n)=v.get("Variable").and_then(|v|v.as_str())&&let Some(e)=bindings.get(n){resolve(e,bindings,depth+1)}else{v}
    }
    let mut out=BTreeSet::new();
    walk(&json,&mut |v|for tag in ["Insert","InsertIfAbsent","Upsert","Update","WriteTarget"]{
        let Some(w)=v.get(tag)else{continue;};let table=w.get("table").or_else(||w.get("target").and_then(|t|t.get("table"))).and_then(|v|v.as_str());
        let Some(payload)=w.get("row").or_else(||w.get("patch"))else{continue;};let payload=resolve(payload,&bindings,0);
        let Some(fields)=payload.get("Object").and_then(|v|v.as_object())else{continue;};
        for inv in bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|Some(i.table.as_str())==table&&i.column.is_some()&&!matches!(i.target.as_str(),"read"|"always")&&i.operation.as_ref().is_none_or(|op|op==&p.name)){
            if let Some(value)=fields.get(inv.column.as_ref().unwrap())&&let Some(arg)=resolve(value,&bindings,0).get("Variable").and_then(|v|v.as_str())&&p.args.contains_key(arg){out.insert(arg.into());}
        }
    });out
}

"""Read-only corpus inputs; every experiment uses a cleaned temporary copy."""
