#[derive(Clone,Debug,Serialize,serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Step {pub operation:String,pub viewer:String,pub args:BTreeMap<String,Value>,pub result:serde_json::Value}

pub(super) fn viewers(bound:&Bound)->Vec<String>{
    let mut out=BTreeSet::from([VIEWER.into(),OTHER.into(),"account:security-no-role".into(),"service:security".into()]);
    out.extend(bound.personas.iter().map(|p|if p.contains(':'){p.clone()}else{format!("dev:{p}")}));
    fn seats(value:&serde_json::Value,out:&mut BTreeSet<String>){match value{
        serde_json::Value::String(s) if s.starts_with("service:")&&s.len()>8=>{out.insert(s.clone());},
        serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs{seats(x,out)},
        serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for x in xs.values(){seats(x,out)},_=>{}
    }}
    seats(&serde_json::to_value(&bound.schema).unwrap(),&mut out);
    for p in &bound.programs{seats(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program).unwrap(),&mut out);}
    seats(&serde_json::to_value(&bound.invariants).unwrap(),&mut out);
    out.into_iter().collect()
}
pub(super) fn actors(bound:&Bound,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>)->Vec<String>{
    let mut out=viewers(bound);
    for (table,rs) in rows{for row in rs{for (c,k) in &bound.schema.tables[table].columns{
        if matches!(k.required(),C::Principal)&&let Ok(Value::Id(p))=row.field(c)&&!out.contains(p){out.push(p.clone());}
    }}}
    out
}

//! Conservative transitive write closure for pre-write policy snapshots.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#127-stable-judgments-and-direct-payload-witnesses — implicit writes cannot establish pre-write intent.
use super::*;
pub(super) fn implicit(bound:&Bound,p:&Program)->BTreeSet<String>{
    let mut affected=ir::write_tables(p).into_iter().map(|(t,_)|t).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    // A plain update cannot trigger an on-delete cascade. Maintains, live
    // read-through retirement and expiring tables can still remove rows.
    let mut removed=ir::write_tables(p).into_iter().filter(|(t,e)|*e=="delete"||bound.schema.tables.get(t).is_some_and(|t|t.is_expiring())).map(|(t,_)|t).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    let mut implicit=BTreeSet::new();
    loop{
        let before=(affected.len(),removed.len());
        for m in &bound.schema.maintains{if affected.contains(&m.source)||m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|r|affected.contains(&r.table)){
            if bound.schema.table(&m.target).is_some(){implicit.insert(m.target.clone());affected.insert(m.target.clone());removed.insert(m.target.clone());}
            if let Some(owner)=&m.private{implicit.insert(owner.table.clone());affected.insert(owner.table.clone());removed.insert(owner.table.clone());}
        }}
        for (name,t) in &bound.schema.tables{
            if t.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|edge|edge.live.is_some()&&affected.contains(&edge.parent)){implicit.insert(name.clone());affected.insert(name.clone());removed.insert(name.clone());}
            for (column,action) in &t.on_delete{
            if action.writes()&&let Some(C::Ref{table})=t.columns.get(column).map(C::required)&&removed.contains(table){implicit.insert(name.clone());affected.insert(name.clone());if matches!(action,snapback4_core::schema::references::OnDelete::Cascade)||t.is_expiring(){removed.insert(name.clone());}}
        }}
        if before==(affected.len(),removed.len()){break;}
    }implicit
}

pub(super) fn dependencies(bound:&Bound,rule:&RuleExpr)->BTreeSet<String>{
    let mut deps=kernel::dependencies(rule);
    loop{let before=deps.len();for name in deps.clone(){if let Some(t)=bound.schema.table(&name){deps.extend(kernel::dependencies(&t.rules.read));if let Some(edge)=&t.through{deps.insert(edge.parent.clone());}}}if before==deps.len(){return deps;}}
}

-- Mobile Notary Signings.
-- Roles: owner (agency owner), dispatcher, notary, title_company.
-- A signing always carries the signer's ID scan and the signing fee.
-- Notaries read operational fields but never the fee or billing notes;
-- only dispatcher/owner read those. Title companies read only their own
-- signings. Status flows requested -> assigned -> signed -> returned, and
-- returned must land within 24h of signing. Only the owner approves a
-- notary for out-of-state papers.
use identity password
use personas alice, bob

-- Roster: exactly one role per principal. Only the local operator
-- (staging/production bootstrap) writes it; app code never self-assigns.
table roles:
  principal: principal
  role: enum('owner', 'dispatcher', 'notary', 'title_company')
  unique principal
  immutable principal
  read <- .principal = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher']
  insert <- viewer = 'service:operator'
  update <- viewer = 'service:operator'
  delete <- viewer = 'service:operator'
  cap 1000
  online only

mutation provision(principal: principal, role: enum('owner', 'dispatcher', 'notary', 'title_company')):
  require viewer = 'service:operator' else NOT_OPERATOR
  return upsert roles[principal] { principal, role }

query myRole():
  return roles[viewer]

-- Out-of-state approval per notary. Notaries register themselves; only the
-- owner flips the approval flag.
table notaryProfiles:
  principal: principal
  approvedOutOfState: bool default false
  unique principal
  immutable principal
  read <- .principal = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher']
  insert <- .principal = viewer
  update <- exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner']
  cap 1000
  online only

mutation registerNotary():
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'notary'] else NOT_NOTARY
  if exists notaryProfiles[principal = viewer]:
    return notaryProfiles[principal = viewer]
  return insert notaryProfiles { principal: viewer }

mutation approveNotary(notary: principal, approved: bool):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_OWNER 'Only the agency owner approves notaries for out-of-state papers.'
  require exists roles[principal = notary, role = 'notary'] else NOT_A_NOTARY 'That principal is not a notary.'
  p = notaryProfiles[principal = notary] ! else NOT_REGISTERED 'That notary has not registered.'
  update notaryProfiles[p.id] { approvedOutOfState: approved }
  return null

query notaryDirectory():
  return roles where .role = 'notary' first 100 by .principal

query approvalDirectory():
  return notaryProfiles first 100 by .principal

table signings:
  titleCompany: principal
  notary: principal ?
  signerName: text 1..120
  address: text 1..300
  documents: [text <=200] 1..20
  idScan: image <=10000000
  fee: money USD
  agencyBillingNotes: text <=2000 ? renamed from billingNotes
  outOfState: bool default false
  status: enum('requested', 'assigned', 'signed', 'returned') default 'requested'
  signedAt: time ?
  returnedAt: time ?
  createdAt: time default now
  immutable titleCompany, createdAt
  read <- exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'notary'] or .titleCompany = viewer
  read (fee, agencyBillingNotes) <- exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher']
  insert <- exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'title_company'] and .titleCompany = viewer
  update <- exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or .notary = viewer
  cap 5000

-- Title companies file signing requests for themselves. The ID scan and the
-- fee are required: omitting either refuses at decode time.
mutation createSigning(signerName: text 1..120, address: text 1..300, documents: [text <=200] 1..20, idScan: image <=10000000, fee: money USD, agencyBillingNotes: text <=2000 ? alias billingNotes, outOfState: bool ?):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'title_company'] else NOT_TITLE_COMPANY
  return insert signings { titleCompany: viewer, signerName, address, documents, idScan, fee, agencyBillingNotes, outOfState: outOfState ?? false }

-- Dispatchers and the owner assign a registered notary. Out-of-state papers
-- need an owner-approved notary.
mutation assignSigning(signing: signings, notary: principal):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_STAFF 'Only dispatch staff assign signings.'
  require exists roles[principal = notary, role = 'notary'] else NOT_A_NOTARY 'That principal is not a notary.'
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'requested' else BAD_STATUS 'Only requested signings can be assigned.'
  if s.outOfState:
    p = notaryProfiles[principal = notary] ! else NOT_APPROVED 'That notary is not approved for out-of-state papers.'
    require p.approvedOutOfState else NOT_APPROVED 'That notary is not approved for out-of-state papers.'
  update signings[signing] { notary, status: 'assigned' }
  return null

-- The assigned notary (or dispatch staff) records the signing.
mutation markSigned(signing: signings):
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'assigned' else BAD_STATUS 'Only assigned signings can be marked signed.'
  require s.notary = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_ASSIGNED 'Only the assigned notary or dispatch staff records the signing.'
  update signings[signing] { status: 'signed', signedAt: now }
  return null

-- Signed papers ship back within one day of signing; later returns refuse.
mutation markReturned(signing: signings):
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'signed' else BAD_STATUS 'Only signed signings can be marked returned.'
  require s.signedAt != null else BAD_STATUS 'This signing has no signing time.'
  require now <= s.signedAt + 24h else RETURN_OVERDUE 'Signed papers must ship back within one day of signing.'
  require s.notary = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_ASSIGNED 'Only the assigned notary or dispatch staff records the return.'
  update signings[signing] { status: 'returned', returnedAt: now }
  return null

-- Dispatch staff adjust the fee charged to the title company. Only the
-- agency owner may change the agency billing notes; the dispatcher may
-- still read them but cannot change them.
mutation updateBilling(signing: signings, fee: money USD, agencyBillingNotes: text <=2000 ? alias billingNotes):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_STAFF 'Only dispatch staff edits billing.'
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  if agencyBillingNotes != s.agencyBillingNotes:
    require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_OWNER_NOTES 'Only the agency owner changes agency billing notes.'
  update signings[signing] { fee, agencyBillingNotes }
  return null

-- Live dispatch board: every caller sees exactly the rows (and columns)
-- their rules admit, newest arrivals last.
query board(c: cursor ?):
  return signings first 100 by .id after c

query signingDetail(signing: signings):
  return signings[signing]

mutation book(site: sites, arrival: time, nights: int 1..30, photo: image <=5000000):
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  s = sites[site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'open' or s.status = 'cleaned' or (s.status = 'booked' and s.holdUntil != null and now >= s.holdUntil) else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  require arrival >= now and arrival <= now + 365d else ARRIVAL_RANGE
  total = s.nightly * nights
  b = insert stays { owner: viewer, site, arrival, nights, total, deposit: s.nightly, status: 'booked', reason: '' }
  insert vehicles { owner: viewer, stay: b.id, photo }
  insert payments { owner: viewer, stay: b.id, charged: total, refunded: 0, forfeited: 0, reason: '' }
  update sites[site] { status: 'booked', current: b.id, holdUntil: arrival + 1d, reason: '' }
  return b

mutation cancel(stay: stays):
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.owner = viewer else PRIVATE_BOOKING
  require b.status = 'booked' else NOT_BOOKED
  require now < b.arrival + 1d else HOLD_EXPIRED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status != 'closed' else RANGER_REFUND_REQUIRED
  lost = b.deposit if b.arrival - now < 14d else 0
  update payments[stay = stay] { refunded: b.total - lost, forfeited: lost, reason: 'Camper cancellation' }
  update stays[stay] { status: 'cancelled', reason: 'Camper cancellation' }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'open', current: null, holdUntil: null }

mutation checkIn(stay: stays):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.status = 'booked' else NOT_BOOKED
  require now >= b.arrival else TOO_EARLY
  require now < b.arrival + 1d else HOLD_EXPIRED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'booked' and s.current = stay else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  update stays[stay] { status: 'occupied' }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'occupied', holdUntil: null }

mutation checkOut(stay: stays):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.status = 'occupied' else NOT_OCCUPIED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'occupied' and s.current = stay else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  update stays[stay] { status: 'completed' }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'dirty', current: null }

mutation clean(site: sites):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  s = sites[site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'dirty' else NOT_DIRTY
  update sites[site] { status: 'cleaned' }

mutation closeSite(site: sites, reason: text 3..500):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(reason)) >= 3 else REASON_REQUIRED
  s = sites[site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status != 'closed' else ALREADY_CLOSED
  update sites[site] { status: 'closed', reason }

mutation refundClosed(stay: stays, reason: text 3..500):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(reason)) >= 3 else REASON_REQUIRED
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'closed' else SITE_NOT_CLOSED
  require b.status = 'booked' or b.status = 'occupied' else NOT_REFUNDABLE
  update payments[stay = stay] { refunded: b.total, forfeited: 0, reason }
  update stays[stay] { status: 'refunded', reason }
  update sites[b.site] { current: null }

mutation evict(stay: stays, reason: text 3..500):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(reason)) >= 3 else REASON_REQUIRED
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.status = 'occupied' else NOT_OCCUPIED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'occupied' and s.current = stay else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  update stays[stay] { status: 'evicted', reason }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'dirty', current: null, reason }

job releaseNoShows():
  for b in stays:
    if b.status = 'booked' and now >= b.arrival + 1d:
      s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
      if s.status != 'closed':
        update stays[b.id] { status: 'released', reason: 'No check-in within one day' }
        if s.current = b.id and s.status = 'booked':
          update sites[b.site] { status: 'open', current: null, holdUntil: null }

schedule noShowSweep every 1m: releaseNoShows

-- v2 renamed the 'inspected' stage to 'inspection recorded'. The column still
-- admits the old value so that every historical row survives adoption and
-- rollback without dormancy; the migrateInspectionRecorded mutation below
-- moves every remaining 'inspected' row to the renamed stage (run after
-- deploy and after every forward), and no workflow mutation writes the old
-- value anymore. Rollback to a release without the renamed value projects
-- 'inspection recorded' back to 'inspected' instead of hiding rows.
down applications inspectedView(status: enum('applied', 'inspected', 'inspection recorded', 'approved', 'failed')): {status: 'inspected' if status = 'inspection recorded' else status}

-- One-shot data migration for the v2 rename. Supervisor-only. Moves a single
-- remaining 'inspected' application to 'inspection recorded'; callers page
-- the board until none remain.
mutation migrateInspectionRecorded(application: applications):
  require exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] else NOT_SUPERVISOR
  app = applications[application] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require app.status = 'inspected' else NOT_INSPECTED
  update applications[app.id] { status: 'inspection recorded' }
  return applications[app.id]

-- Inspections are written by inspectors (or supervisors). owner is the truck
-- owner's principal, denormalized so operators read their own reports and
-- staff read everything.
table inspections:
  truck: trucks
  application: applications ?
  permit: permits ?
  inspector: principal
  passed: bool
  notes: text <=2000 ?
  kind: enum('initial', 'reinspection', 'routine')
  inspectedAt: time default now
  owner: principal
  immutable truck, application, permit, inspector, passed, notes, kind, inspectedAt, owner
  read <- .owner = viewer or exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor']
  insert <- exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor']
  online only

-- First inspection of an application: applied -> inspection recorded.
mutation inspectApplication(application: applications, passed: bool, notes: text <=2000 ?):
  require exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] else NOT_INSPECTOR
  app = applications[application] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require app.status = 'applied' else NOT_APPLIED
  i = insert inspections { truck: app.truck, application: app.id, inspector: viewer, passed, notes, kind: 'initial', owner: app.owner }
  update applications[app.id] { status: 'inspection recorded', lastPassed: passed }
  return i

-- Reinspection of a failed application, only within ten days of the failure.
mutation reinspectApplication(application: applications, passed: bool, notes: text <=2000 ?):
  require exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] else NOT_INSPECTOR
  app = applications[application] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require app.status = 'failed' else NOT_FAILED
  require now <= app.failedAt + 10d else REINSPECTION_LATE
  i = insert inspections { truck: app.truck, application: app.id, inspector: viewer, passed, notes, kind: 'reinspection', owner: app.owner }
  update applications[app.id] { status: 'inspection recorded', lastPassed: passed }
  return i

-- Decision on an inspection-recorded application. Approval issues the permit, valid
-- 365 days; rejection marks it failed and starts the ten-day reinspection
-- window.
mutation approveApplication(application: applications):
  require exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] else NOT_INSPECTOR
  app = applications[application] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require app.status = 'inspection recorded' else NOT_INSPECTED
  require app.lastPassed else DECISION_CONFLICTS
  p = insert permits { truck: app.truck, owner: app.owner, application: app.id, issuedAt: now, expiresAt: now + 365d, status: 'active', flagged: false, failedAt: now }
  update applications[app.id] { status: 'approved' }
  update trucks[app.truck] { activePermit: p.id }
  return p

mutation rejectApplication(application: applications):
  require exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] else NOT_INSPECTOR
  app = applications[application] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require app.status = 'inspection recorded' else NOT_INSPECTED
  require not app.lastPassed else DECISION_CONFLICTS
  update applications[app.id] { status: 'failed', failedAt: now }
  return applications[app.id]

-- Routine inspection (or reinspection) of an active permit.
mutation inspectPermit(permit: permits, passed: bool, notes: text <=2000 ?):
  require exists roster[viewer, role = 'inspector'] or exists roster[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] else NOT_INSPECTOR
  p = permits[permit] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require p.status = 'active' else PERMIT_NOT_ACTIVE
  require now < p.expiresAt else PERMIT_EXPIRED
  i = insert inspections { truck: p.truck, permit: p.id, inspector: viewer, passed, notes, kind: 'reinspection' if p.flagged else 'routine', owner: p.owner }
  update permits[p.id] { flagged: not passed, failedAt: now }
  return i

-- Daily sweep: suspend active flagged permits whose reinspection window
-- lapsed, and expire permits past their 365-day life.
job sweepPermits(periodStart: time, periodEnd: time):
  for p in permits:
    if p.status = 'active' and p.flagged and p.failedAt < periodEnd - 10d:
      update permits[p.id] { status: 'suspended', flagged: false }
      insert suspensions { permit: p.id, owner: p.owner, reason: 'No passing reinspection within ten days of the failed inspection.', suspendedAt: periodEnd }
      upsert operatorFlags[p.owner] { operator: p.owner, suspended: true }
    if p.status = 'active' and p.expiresAt <= periodEnd:
      update permits[p.id] { status: 'expired', flagged: false }

schedule dailySweep every 1d at 03:00: sweepPermits

-- The dispatcher opens each job with the ownership/lease photo and the quoted
-- charge, or without a charge when none has been quoted yet. A lockout job
-- carries no photo and must stay booked until the owner approves it. Overdue
-- is stamped at opening: scheduled more than seven days after the request.
mutation openJob(customer: principal, address: text 1..200, detail: text <=500 ?, proof: image <=10MB ?, quoted: money USD ?, scheduledAt: time, lockout: bool):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_DISPATCHER 'Only the dispatcher or owner may open jobs.'
  require quoted = null or quoted >= 1 else BAD_QUOTE 'The quoted charge must be positive.'
  require scheduledAt >= now else BAD_SCHEDULE 'The job must be scheduled for now or later.'
  require (lockout and proof = null) or (not lockout and proof != null) else BAD_PROOF_STATE 'Ordinary jobs need the ownership photo; lockout jobs must omit it.'
  req = now
  return insert jobs { customer, address, detail, proof, quoted, status: 'booked', requestedAt: req, scheduledAt, lockout, overdue: scheduledAt > req + 7d }

-- Spec: only the dispatcher or owner enters or revises the quoted charge;
-- customers and locksmiths cannot. A job opened before quoting carries a null
-- quote until this runs.
invariant jobs.setQuoted only exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner']

mutation setQuoted(job: jobs, quoted: money USD):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_DISPATCHER 'Only the dispatcher or owner may quote jobs.'
  j = jobs[job] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require quoted >= 1 else BAD_QUOTE 'The quoted charge must be positive.'
  update jobs[job] { quoted }
  return null

-- Spec: only staff move jobs, strictly booked -> onsite -> done; a lockout
-- without proof needs the owner's approval before onsite or done; completing
-- stamps the 30-day free-recut deadline.
-- Spec: only the owner approves a lockout without proof (see approveLockout).
invariant jobs.setJobStatus only exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'locksmith'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner']
invariant jobs.approveLockout only exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner']

mutation setJobStatus(job: jobs, status: enum('booked', 'onsite', 'done')):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'locksmith'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_STAFF 'Only shop staff may move jobs.'
  j = jobs[job] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require (j.status = 'booked' and status = 'onsite') or (j.status = 'onsite' and status = 'done') else BAD_TRANSITION 'Jobs move booked to onsite to done.'
  if j.lockout and j.proof = null:
    require j.approvalReason != null else NEEDS_LOCKOUT_APPROVAL 'A lockout without proof needs the owner approval first.'
  if status = 'done':
    stamp = now
    update jobs[job] { status, completedAt: stamp, recutDeadline: stamp + 30d }
  else:
    update jobs[job] { status }
  return null

-- Only the shop owner approves a lockout without ownership proof, recording
-- the reason and a witness name.
mutation approveLockout(job: jobs, reason: text 1..300, witness: text 1..80):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_OWNER 'Only the shop owner may approve a lockout.'
  j = jobs[job] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require j.lockout and j.proof = null else NOT_LOCKOUT 'Only a lockout without proof needs approval.'
  require j.approvalReason = null else ALREADY_APPROVED 'This lockout is already approved.'
  update jobs[job] { approvalReason: reason, approvalWitness: witness, approvedBy: viewer }
  return null

//! Finite three-valued implication, deliberately independent of database facts.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#3-sound-proof-boundary — impossible valuations overapproximate all snapshots.
use snapback4_core::schema::{RuleExpr as R, RuleTerm as T};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

pub const MAX_ATOMS: usize = 10;
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Truth { Yes, No, Unknown }
impl Truth {
    fn not(self) -> Self { match self { Self::Yes => Self::No, Self::No => Self::Yes, Self::Unknown => Self::Unknown } }
    fn combine(self, other: Self, and: bool) -> Self {
        let decisive = if and { Self::No } else { Self::Yes };
        if self == decisive || other == decisive { decisive }
        else if self == Self::Unknown || other == Self::Unknown { Self::Unknown }
        else { decisive.not() }
    }
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
enum Formula { Constant(Truth), Atom(usize), Not(Box<Self>), And(Vec<Self>), Or(Vec<Self>) }
impl Formula {
    fn eval(&self, values: &[Truth]) -> Truth {
        match self {
            Self::Constant(v) => *v, Self::Atom(n) => values[*n], Self::Not(x) => x.eval(values).not(),
            Self::And(xs) => xs.iter().fold(Truth::Yes, |v, x| v.combine(x.eval(values), true)),
            Self::Or(xs) => xs.iter().fold(Truth::No, |v, x| v.combine(x.eval(values), false)),
        }
    }
}
fn term(t: &T) -> T { match t { T::NextField(f) => T::Field(f.clone()), other => other.clone() } }
fn atom(rule: &R) -> String {
    let mut r = rule.clone();
    match &mut r {
        R::Eq(a,b) | R::Compare(_,a,b) => { *a=term(a); *b=term(b); }
        R::Exists { key, equalities, .. } | R::Created { key, equalities, .. } => {
            for t in key { *t=term(t); }
            for (_,t) in equalities.iter_mut() { *t=term(t); }
            equalities.sort_by(|a,b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    if let R::Eq(a,b)=&mut r && serde_json::to_string(a).unwrap()>serde_json::to_string(b).unwrap() { std::mem::swap(a,b); }
    let mut json=serde_json::to_value(&r).unwrap();
    // Provenance controls planning, not rule evaluation. Remove only this
    // leaf's metadata, never a similarly named literal-object field.
    for name in ["Exists","Created"] { if let Some(body)=json.get_mut(name).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_object_mut) { body.remove("provenance"); } }
    json.to_string()
}
fn formula(rule: &R, atoms: &mut Vec<String>, nodes: &mut usize) -> Result<Formula, String> {
    *nodes+=1; if *nodes>1024 { return Err("formula exceeds 1024 nodes".into()); }
    Ok(match rule {
        R::Allow | R::Public {..} => Formula::Constant(Truth::Yes), R::Deny => Formula::Constant(Truth::No),
        R::And(xs) => Formula::And(xs.iter().map(|r| formula(r,atoms,nodes)).collect::<Result<_,_>>()?),
        R::Or(xs) => Formula::Or(xs.iter().map(|r| formula(r,atoms,nodes)).collect::<Result<_,_>>()?),
        R::Not(x) => Formula::Not(Box::new(formula(x,atoms,nodes)?)),
        R::Ne(a,b) => Formula::Not(Box::new(formula(&R::Eq(a.clone(),b.clone()),atoms,nodes)?)),
        R::Eq(T::Literal(a),T::Literal(b)) => Formula::Constant(if a==b {Truth::Yes}else{Truth::No}),
        R::Eq(T::Viewer,T::Viewer) => Formula::Constant(Truth::Yes),
        other => { let key=atom(other); let n=atoms.iter().position(|a| a==&key).unwrap_or_else(|| {atoms.push(key);atoms.len()-1});
            if atoms.len()>MAX_ATOMS {return Err(format!("more than {MAX_ATOMS} independent predicates"));} Formula::Atom(n) }
    })
}
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#133-coverage-and-bounded-checking — exact inputs only; no fixture assumptions.
thread_local! {
    static IMPLICATIONS: std::cell::RefCell<std::collections::BTreeMap<String,Result<bool,String>>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(std::collections::BTreeMap::new()) };
}
/// Only exact kernel implication results are reused, never concrete judgments.
pub fn implies(admission: &R, policy: &R) -> Result<bool,String> {
    let key=serde_json::to_string(&(admission,policy)).unwrap();
    if let Some(result)=IMPLICATIONS.with(|cache|cache.borrow().get(&key).cloned()){return result;}
    let result=uncached(admission,policy);
    IMPLICATIONS.with(|cache|{let mut cache=cache.borrow_mut();if cache.len()>=4096{cache.clear();}cache.insert(key,result.clone());});
    result
}
fn uncached(admission: &R, policy: &R) -> Result<bool,String> {
    let (mut atoms,mut nodes)=(Vec::new(),0);
    let a=formula(admission,&mut atoms,&mut nodes)?;
    let p=formula(policy,&mut atoms,&mut nodes)?;
    let mut values=vec![Truth::Unknown;atoms.len()];
    for mut n in 0..3usize.pow(atoms.len() as u32) {
        for v in &mut values { *v=match n%3 {0=>Truth::Yes,1=>Truth::No,_=>Truth::Unknown}; n/=3; }
        if a.eval(&values)==Truth::Yes && p.eval(&values)!=Truth::Yes { return Ok(false); }
    }
    Ok(true)
}
pub fn dependencies(rule: &R) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut out=BTreeSet::new();
    match rule {
        R::Exists{table,key,equalities,..}|R::Created{table,key,equalities,..} => {out.insert(table.clone());for term in key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_,t)|t)){for (table,_) in term.references(){out.insert(table.into());}}}
        R::And(xs)|R::Or(xs) => for x in xs {out.extend(dependencies(x));}, R::Not(x) => out.extend(dependencies(x)),
        R::Eq(a,b)|R::Ne(a,b)|R::Compare(_,a,b) => for t in [a,b] { for (table,_) in t.references() {out.insert(table.into());} },
        _=>{}
    }
    out
}

//! Review questions describe enforcement; they never infer specification intent.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#131-intent-and-diagnostics — advisory comparisons do not change proof statuses or authority.
use super::*;
use snapback4_core::{schema::{ColumnType,Table},Value};

pub(super) fn roles(bound:&Bound)->Vec<String>{
    let mut roles=BTreeSet::new();
    for (name,table) in bound.schema.visible_tables(){
        let mut columns=super::privilege::role_columns(bound,name);
        // Scoped memberships have the same questionnaire need as global roles.
        // Require an observed caller probe; an event's `kind` plus `author`
        // is not enough to invent a role roster.
        for (_,other) in bound.schema.visible_tables(){for rule in super::columns::rules(other){
            let mut parts=Vec::new();leaves(rule,&mut parts);
            for part in parts{if let RuleExpr::Exists{table:roster,index,key,equalities,..}=part&&roster==name{
                let pairs=super::privilege::probe_pairs(bound,roster,index,key,equalities);
                if pairs.iter().any(|(c,v)|matches!(v,RuleTerm::Viewer)&&matches!(table.columns.get(c).map(ColumnType::required),Some(ColumnType::Principal))){
                    columns.extend(pairs.iter().filter(|(c,v)|matches!(c.as_str(),"role"|"kind")&&matches!(v,RuleTerm::Literal(Value::String(_)))).map(|(c,_)|c.clone()));
                }
            }}
        }}
        for column in columns {for value in super::privilege::role_values(bound,name,&column){
            roles.insert(format!("{name}.{column} = '{value}'"));
        }}
    }
    roles.into_iter().collect()
}

pub(super) fn row_context(table:&Table)->String{
    let mut relationships=Vec::new();let mut states=Vec::new();
    for (column,kind) in &table.columns {
        match kind.required(){
            ColumnType::Principal=>relationships.push(format!(".{column} (principal)")),
            ColumnType::Ref{table}=>relationships.push(format!(".{column} ({table})")),
            ColumnType::Enum{variants}=>states.push(format!(".{column}: {}",variants.join(" / "))),
            _=>{},
        }
    }
    format!("relationships: {}; state/category values: {}. Confirm their meaning from the spec.",
        if relationships.is_empty(){"none declared".into()}else{relationships.join(", ")},
        if states.is_empty(){"none declared".into()}else{states.join(", ")})
}

/// Bounded distribution retains each AND condition when showing OR audiences.
/// Oversized formulas stay whole; no branch or condition is silently dropped.
fn alternatives(rule:&RuleExpr)->Vec<RuleExpr>{
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Or(xs)=>{
            let out=xs.iter().flat_map(alternatives).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if out.len()>32{vec![rule.clone()]}else{out}
        },
        RuleExpr::And(xs)=>{
            let mut out=vec![Vec::new()];
            for x in xs {
                let next=alternatives(x);
                if out.len().saturating_mul(next.len())>32{return vec![rule.clone()];}
                out=out.into_iter().flat_map(|prefix|next.iter().map(move |part|{
                    let mut parts=prefix.clone();parts.push(part.clone());parts
                })).collect();
            }
            out.into_iter().map(RuleExpr::And).collect()
        },
        other=>vec![other.clone()],
    }
}
fn leaves<'a>(rule:&'a RuleExpr,out:&mut Vec<&'a RuleExpr>){match rule{
    RuleExpr::And(xs)|RuleExpr::Or(xs)=>for x in xs{leaves(x,out)},
    RuleExpr::Not(x)=>leaves(x,out),r=>out.push(r),
}}
fn audience(bound:&Bound,rule:&RuleExpr)->String{
    let mut actors=BTreeSet::new();
    fn collect(bound:&Bound,rule:&RuleExpr,actors:&mut BTreeSet<String>){match rule{
        // Negated role tests are conditions, not an admitted role.
        RuleExpr::And(xs)=>for x in xs{collect(bound,x,actors)},
        RuleExpr::Exists{table,index,key,equalities,..}=>{
            let pairs=super::privilege::probe_pairs(bound,table,index,key,equalities);
            if !pairs.iter().any(|(_,v)|matches!(v,RuleTerm::Viewer)){return;}
            let columns=super::privilege::role_columns(bound,table);
            let mut named=false;
            for (c,v) in &pairs{if columns.contains(c)||matches!(c.as_str(),"role"|"kind"){
                if let RuleTerm::Literal(Value::String(value))=v{actors.insert(format!("{table}.{c} = '{value}'"));named=true;}
            }}
            if !named{actors.insert(format!("a caller with a matching {table} relationship"));}
        },
        RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer,term)|RuleExpr::Eq(term,RuleTerm::Viewer)=>{
            actors.insert(format!("a caller satisfying {}",RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer,term.clone()).quarry()));
        },_=>{},
    }}
    collect(bound,rule,&mut actors);
    if actors.is_empty(){"a signed-in caller satisfying this branch".into()}else{actors.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" and ")}
}

pub(super) fn questions(bound:&Bound,target:&str,effect:&str,gate:&RuleExpr)->String{
    alternatives(gate).iter().filter(|branch|kernel::implies(branch,&RuleExpr::Deny)!=Ok(true)).map(|branch|{
        let actor=audience(bound,branch);
        let mut fields=BTreeSet::new();branch.fields(&mut fields);
        let image_fields=branch.any_term(&|t|matches!(t,RuleTerm::OldField(_)|RuleTerm::NextField(_)));
        let scope=if fields.is_empty()&&!image_fields{"no row relationship or lifecycle condition in this branch".to_owned()}
            else if fields.is_empty(){"row-image conditions shown in the branch".into()}
            else{format!("row conditions on {}",fields.iter().map(|f|format!(".{f}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))};
        format!("{}Rule {target}.{effect} admits {actor} under `{}` ({scope}). Should the spec allow this audience on these rows and columns, including other people's rows and every lifecycle state?",if matches!(effect,"insert"|"update"|"delete"|"write"){format!("May any {actor} write any {target} row, or only the owner of THIS resource? ")}else{String::new()},branch.quarry())
    }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")
}

/// Lint-only normalization. It is never used by the proof or a counterexample.
/// Named-key probes with extra equalities imply the same probe with fewer
/// equalities; an existing row's self-id probe repeats its own current fields.
fn normalized(bound:&Bound,target:&str,current_read:bool,rule:&RuleExpr)->RuleExpr{
    match rule{
        RuleExpr::And(xs)=>RuleExpr::And(xs.iter().map(|r|normalized(bound,target,current_read,r)).collect()),
        RuleExpr::Or(xs)=>RuleExpr::Or(xs.iter().map(|r|normalized(bound,target,current_read,r)).collect()),
        RuleExpr::Not(x)=>RuleExpr::Not(Box::new(normalized(bound,target,current_read,x))),
        RuleExpr::Exists{table,index,key,equalities,..}=>{
            let mut pairs=super::privilege::probe_pairs(bound,table,index,key,equalities);
            pairs.sort_by_key(|(c,t)|(c.clone(),serde_json::to_string(t).unwrap()));pairs.dedup();
            if current_read&&table==target&&pairs.contains(&("id".into(),RuleTerm::Field("id".into()))) {
                RuleExpr::And(pairs.into_iter().filter(|(c,t)|c!="id"||t!=&RuleTerm::Field("id".into()))
                    .map(|(c,t)|RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Field(c),t)).collect())
            }else{
                RuleExpr::Exists{table:table.clone(),index:"$advisory-named-pairs".into(),key:Vec::new(),equalities:pairs,provenance:snapback4_core::ir::KeyProvenance::Computed}
            }
        },_=>rule.clone(),
    }
}
fn probe_implies(a:&RuleExpr,b:&RuleExpr)->bool{match(a,b){
    (RuleExpr::Exists{table:a,equalities:ap,..},RuleExpr::Exists{table:b,equalities:bp,..})=>a==b&&bp.iter().all(|p|ap.contains(p)),_=>false,
}}
fn enrich(rule:&RuleExpr,candidates:&[&RuleExpr])->RuleExpr{match rule{
    RuleExpr::And(xs)=>RuleExpr::And(xs.iter().map(|r|enrich(r,candidates)).collect()),
    RuleExpr::Or(xs)=>RuleExpr::Or(xs.iter().map(|r|enrich(r,candidates)).collect()),
//! Effective column payload audience; unresolved observer edges stay explicit.
use super::*;
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#121-column-read-intent — a private owner gate narrows only the column payload.
pub(super) fn admission(table:&snapback4_core::schema::Table,column:Option<&str>)->RuleExpr{
    let mut rules=vec![super::temporal::admission(table)];
    if let Some(owner)=column.and_then(|c|table.written_by.get(c)).filter(|o|!o.audience){
        rules.push(RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Field(owner.owner.clone()),RuleTerm::Viewer));
    }
    if let Some(rule)=column.and_then(|c|table.column_reads.get(c)) { rules.push(rule.clone()); }
    RuleExpr::And(rules)
}

/// Every enforcement gate can confer authority or introduce a raw witness edge.
pub(super) fn rules(table:&snapback4_core::schema::Table)->impl Iterator<Item=&RuleExpr>{
    [&table.rules.read,&table.rules.insert,&table.rules.update,&table.rules.delete].into_iter().chain(table.column_reads.values())
}

/// Column effects carry effective row/owner authority, not a standalone cell gate.
pub(super) fn effects(table:&snapback4_core::schema::Table)->impl Iterator<Item=(String,RuleExpr)>+'_ {
    [("read".into(),table.rules.read.clone()),("insert".into(),table.rules.insert.clone()),("update".into(),table.rules.update.clone()),("delete".into(),table.rules.delete.clone())].into_iter()
        .chain(table.column_reads.keys().map(|column|(format!("{column} read"),admission(table,Some(column)))))
}

-- Staff take a machine back. Returned more than one day late, the contractor
-- is charged another day at the rental's daily price.
mutation returnMachine(rental: rentals, damageFound: bool, damageNote: text <=500 ?, returnPhoto: image <=10000000 ?):
  isStaff = exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'yardhand'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'manager']
  require isStaff else NOT_STAFF 'Only yard staff can take returns.'
  r = rentals[rental] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require r.returnedAt = null else ALREADY_RETURNED 'This rental was already returned.'
  update rentals[rental] { returnedAt: now, damageFound, damageNote }
  update machines[r.machine] { status: 'returned' }
  if returnPhoto != null:
    insert rentalPhotos { rental: r.id, kind: 'return', photo: returnPhoto }
  if now > r.dueAt + 1d:
    insert invoices { rental: r.id, contractor: r.contractor, kind: 'late', amount: r.dailyPrice }
  return null

/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:222:### 2.4 Why the visibility gap persists: Convex makes the bridge mandatory, Snapback makes it optional
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:224:- **On Convex** a strict v1 schema refuses to deploy over v2 data. So wherever the day-one schema could not hold v2's values, the Convex twin wrote a compatibility v1: 003-C `widenRollbackSchema`, 023-C `v1/release`, 035-C `v1-compatible/`, 015-C `.releases/v1`.
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:225:  - 015-C's adds "optional fee fields, acceptance of v2's `fee` audit action, and rejection of refunds for unconfirmed fees". That is a loosened bridge *with v2's safeguard carried over*.
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:226:  - It costs 412 min in 43 lanes, the "strict schema rejects pristine v1" cluster, and 28 of 50 Convex "fix first" votes.
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:228:- **On Snapback** rollback to exact v1 always succeeds, hides what doesn't fit, and restores it on forward. The bridge is the same idea, made optional and cheaper (8 lanes chose it).
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:234:   - When `deploy` (and `deploy --check`) finds a domain widening that an earlier still-selectable release can't hold, it generates the loosened bridge in memory, compiles it, and **registers it as that release's rollback view** (`rollback --to 1` selects "release 1 via bridge N"; `--exact` selects the original).
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:239:   - For each v1 operation that reads a loosened column as required, carry v2's guard on it (`require a.amount != null else …`) instead of proposing `?? 0` (`release_bridge.rs:21`, `:51`).
/home/ccheever/sb4-loop/wave23/analysis/bakeoff-day2.md:241:   - Cut the checklist to the loosened columns, the v1 operations that read them, and the v2 guards carried. Leave the rest to `deploy --check`.

**Did builders see SEC6's `deploy --check` security review items?** Almost never, and the format is why.
- A rule-changing deploy prints `SECURITY REVIEW — rules changed` and `last test:` (`snapback4/src/verbs/security.rs:82-103`). It lists every note, unranked and uncapped (`:96`), on stderr, with `N_COLUMN_RESULT_EXPOSURE` last. "Rule-changing" means any table's rules changed (`:83`), so every deploy in this wave qualifies.
- **Direct `deploy --check`: 36 runs in 27 lanes. None was viewed in full.** Builders read them through `grep -v review` (6), `--json` (11), `tail`/`head` (11) or a file (8).
- **Plain `deploy`: 70 runs, 4 viewed in full.** The rest went through `tail` 34, `--json` 21, a file 9, `grep -v review` 2.
- Six lanes filtered review lines explicitly: 002, 003, 004, 018, 040, 049. For example, 003 ran `grep -vE "REVIEW|confirm the spec|…|last test"`.
- 47 deploy/rollback outputs in 34 lanes showed some REVIEW lines. Because builders `tail`, most showed only the trailing `N_COLUMN_RESULT_EXPOSURE` notes.
- `last test:` read NEVER RECORDED in 23 lanes and STALE in 6.
- Day two ran `test` 6 times in 3 lanes (033, 035, 048) and `audit` once (032). Nobody ran `deploy --strict`. 64 invariant lines were added or edited in 32 lanes, all spot-checked ones mirrors.

NOT READY

- **Required child media still gates intentional optional attachments.** [§16.9](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b22-sec7/llp/3000.036.004-security-invariants-and-exposure.rfc.md:2317) retains a gate whenever the child’s media column is required and rejects child-local non-null guards as suppression. Wave-23 040’s `returnMachine` intentionally accepts optional `returnPhoto`, inserting `rentalPhotos` only when supplied; `rentalPhotos.photo` is required. The proposed rule therefore preserves this false gate. A required child field establishes validity of an existing attachment, not an obligation to create one—the distinction already recognized by the evidence-removal paragraph. Exclude intentional conditional attachment creation unless parent-level evidence necessity is independently established. Add a negative control for 040’s exact shape alongside the required-child positive control.
